# Drag and drop,<br>built for Vue.

Sortable lists, kanban boards, trees and multi-drag for Vue 3 — animated, keyboard-ready and accessible out of the box.

npm i @vue-dnd-kit/core

[Get started](https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/getting-started/introduction)

Free and open source. MIT licensed.

00How it works

## Composables,<br>not components.

Your markup, your styles. Hand a template ref to a composable and the element drags, sorts and drops — with the animation, keyboard and screen reader work done for you.

- 01 `**makeSortableList**`Lists, grids and kanban columns that reorder as you drag — and trade items within a group.
- 02 `**makeSortableTree**`Nested data, rendered flat: depth by a sideways nudge, drops into folders, virtualization.
- 03 `**makeDraggable · makeDroppable**`Anything else: boards, canvases, uploads — your own rules for what goes where.

01Drag & drop

## Drag and drop

A draggable, a drop target and a rule for what goes where. Targets light up when they take the drag and refuse what they don't; what a drop does is up to you.

[Docs](https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/drag-and-drop)

02Sortable

## Lists and grids

Render a draft of your array and it reorders live while you drag. On drop, the new order is written into your ref. Vertical, horizontal or a grid of any size.

[Docs](https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/sortable-lists)

Live Rearrange the apps, or move one into the dock X ---- · Y ----

Loading the demo…

03Kanban

## Kanban boards

Lists in one group trade items. Copy from a palette, take plain draggables in, or swap instead of shifting — the receiving list makes room as you hover.

[Docs](https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/shared-lists)

Live Move cards between the columns X ---- · Y ----

Loading the demo…

04Trees

## Trees

Rendered flat with depths, so they virtualize. Drag sideways to change the level or hover a folder to drop inside; limit depth and decide what nests where.

[Docs](https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/trees)

Live Drag sideways to change the depth X ---- · Y ----

Loading the demo…

05Multi-drag

## Multi-drag

Select with Ctrl/Cmd-click or draw a box, then drag one: the whole selection travels together and lands in order, even across lists.

[Docs](https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/multi-drag)

Live Ctrl/Cmd-click or draw a box, then drag X ---- · Y ----

06Constraints

## Axes, bounds and grids

A drag area sets the rules for everything dragged inside it: lock an axis, keep drags within its edges, snap to a grid — and change them while the app runs.

[Docs](https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/constraints)

## Ready for real apps.

01

### Animated

FLIP while sorting, a drop that lands on its slot, data changes that animate. Bring GSAP or motion if you like.

02

### Accessible

Keyboard drags by slots, live announcements and ARIA attributes that never override yours.

03

### Virtual lists

TanStack Virtual and VueUse: thousands of rows, still sortable, still animated.

04

### Controlled

Pinia, a server or immutable data: skip the default write and apply the result yourself.

## The core

<code-group>

```bash [npm]
npm i @vue-dnd-kit/core
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add @vue-dnd-kit/core
```

```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add @vue-dnd-kit/core
```

```bash [bun]
bun add @vue-dnd-kit/core
```

</code-group>

Vue `^3.5` is a peer dependency. The package has one dependency of its own, `@vueuse/core`.

## Nuxt

The Nuxt module registers `DnDProvider` and `DragPreview` as global components and
auto-imports the composables and the main types.

```bash
npx nuxi module add @vue-dnd-kit/nuxt
```

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@vue-dnd-kit/nuxt'],
});
```

<note>

Modifiers, collision helpers and sensors have generic names (`snapToGrid`, `closestCenter`), so
they aren't auto-imported unless you ask for them:
`vueDndKit: { autoImports: { modifiers: true, collision: true, sensors: true } }`.

</note>

- **Page:** Lists that share items
- **Source:** https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/shared-lists
- **Description:** Lists in one group move, copy and swap items — the whole column takes drops, pull and put decide what goes in and out, palettes copy, and controlled lists apply each drop to a store with an undo history.

<example height="31rem" hint="Move stories between the lists; switch the drop area off and on" name="sprint-planning">



</example>

## A group

Lists with the same `group` name exchange items. By default every list is a group of its
own.

```vue [Column.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { toRef, useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeSortableList } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';
import StoryCard from './StoryCard.vue';

type Story = { id: string; title: string; points: number };
const props = defineProps<{ column: { id: string; title: string; stories: Story[] } }>();

const list = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('list');
const { items, isOver } = makeSortableList(list, {
  id: props.column.id,                     // names the list in drop events
  items: toRef(props.column, 'stories'),   // a writable ref into the reactive column
  group: 'planning',                       // same name: stories move between these lists
});
</script>

<template>
  <section :class="{ over: isOver }">
    <h3>{{ column.title }}</h3>
    <ul ref="list">
      <StoryCard v-for="story in items" :key="story.id" :story="story" />
    </ul>
  </section>
</template>
```

```vue [index.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { reactive } from 'vue';
import Column from './Column.vue';

const columns = reactive([
  { id: 'backlog', title: 'Backlog', stories: [{ id: 's1', title: 'Saved searches', points: 5 }] },
  { id: 'sprint', title: 'Sprint 14', stories: [] },
]);
</script>

<template>
  <Column v-for="column in columns" :key="column.id" :column="column" />
</template>
```

- Each column is a component here, as columns usually are. One component may also make
several lists, a fixed Todo and Done side by side: each card joins the list whose
element holds it.
- `toRef(props.column, 'stories')` is writable because the parent passes a reactive
object. The drop writes both arrays, the one the story left and the one it entered, and
the points of both columns follow.
- `id` shows up in drop events as `from.list` and `to.list`, and keys `e.result`, the new
arrays of every list the drop changes. `id` and `group` are read once.
- Keys must be unique across the whole group.

A list's `onDrop` runs for the drops **into** it. A move from `backlog` to `sprint` calls
the `sprint` list's `onDrop`, and its `e.result` holds the new arrays of both lists.

## The whole column takes drops: `dropzone`

A short list in a tall column leaves empty space below the last card. With `dropzone`,
another element takes the drops for the list: here the whole column. A story let go
below the last one lands at the end. The stories stay in the `<ul>`; only the area that
takes drops grows. The demo outlines that area while you drag: switch it off, and only
the list itself takes the story.

```ts [Column.vue]
const zone = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('zone');
const { items } = makeSortableList(list, {
  items: toRef(props.column, 'stories'),
  group: 'planning',
  dropzone: zone,   // or a getter: () => (wholeColumn.value ? zone.value : undefined)
});
```

<tip>

Without a `dropzone`, an empty list still needs a size to take drops: give it a
`min-height`.

</tip>

## What goes in and out: `pull` and `put`

`group` also takes an object. `pull` says what may leave a list, `put` what may come in:

<example height="36rem" hint="Drag files between the lists: each one says if it takes them, and why not" name="group-rules">



</example>

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Option
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Values
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        pull
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        true
      </code>
      
       (default): items can leave. <code>
        false
      </code>
      
      : they can't. <code>
        'clone'
      </code>
      
      : copies leave, the items stay.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        put
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        true
      </code>
      
       (default): items can come in. <code>
        false
      </code>
      
      : nothing comes in. A type or types (<code>
        'image'
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        ['image', 'video']
      </code>
      
      ): items of those types come in. A function: you decide per drag.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

```ts [index.vue]
// Inbox: gives, takes nothing.
group: { name: 'files', pull: true, put: false }

// Templates: gives copies, takes nothing, keeps its order.
group: { name: 'files', pull: 'clone', put: false }, sort: false

// Images: takes images only.
group: { name: 'files', put: 'image' }
```

Types are the `type` options of the dragged items (`makeSortableItem(el, { item, type })`);
items without one count as the group's name. With types in `put`, every dragged item must
have one of them (with `acceptMode: 'some'`, the ones that do come in).

A `put` function gets `{ keys, items, types, from, to }`: the dragged keys and items,
their types, the list they come from (`null` for plain draggables) and this list. Moves
inside a list are always allowed: the Inbox still sorts its own files.

Over a list that refuses the drag, the slot goes back to where the drag started, so the
lists show what a drop would do: nothing. A drop there is cancelled and the item flies
back. The list's `isAccepting` is `false` during such a drag, and `isOver` still `true`
over it: that is how each list in the demo knows what to say.

The slot goes home over a drop target of its own outside the lists too, such as a trash
can: the drop there is the target's, and the lists keep the item unless its `onDrop` takes
it out (`event.source.remove()`). Targets inside the lists (a drop into an item) and
around them (a panel holding the lists) leave the slot where it is.

```ts [RuleList.vue]
const { items, isOver, isAccepting } = makeSortableList(el, { … });
const { active } = useDnD();
const verdict = computed(() => (active.value ? (isAccepting.value ? 'takes' : 'refuses') : null));
```

### Limits

A list that holds three files at most, the Shortlist:

```ts [index.vue]
const shortlist = reactive({
  files: [/* … */],
  group: { name: 'files', put: ({ keys }: SortablePutContext) => shortlist.files.length + keys.length <= 3 },
});
```

It reads its own items when a drag asks. Fill it, and it refuses the next file, with the
reason in its header.

When several selected items of different types are dragged, `acceptMode` says whether
`'all'` (default) or `'some'` of them must pass `put`. With `'some'`, the ones that pass
land and the others fly back. See [multi-drag](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/multi-drag#taking-only-some).

### One group per list

A list belongs to one group: `group` takes one name, never several. The lists of a group
share each drag (their drafts, what is dragged, which of them take it), so items never move
between groups. When items should flow only some ways, put the lists in one group and let
`put` decide by `from`, the list a drag comes from:

```ts [index.vue]
// Review takes tasks from both teams. A team takes tasks back from Review,
// never from the other team.
const fromReview = ({ from }: SortablePutContext) => from === 'review';

makeSortableList(review, { id: 'review', items: reviewTasks, group: 'tasks' });
makeSortableList(frontend, { id: 'frontend', items: frontendTasks, group: { name: 'tasks', put: fromReview } });
makeSortableList(backend, { id: 'backend', items: backendTasks, group: { name: 'tasks', put: fromReview } });
```

<note>

Coming from SortableJS: there `put: ['a', 'b']` names the groups a list takes items from.
Here an array in `put` lists the **types** of the items a list takes. To take items from
other lists, give them one group and decide by `from`, as above.

</note>

## Copy: palettes and the Alt key

<example height="26rem" hint="Drag from the palette; Alt-drag copies; drop outside the Page panel to remove" name="palette">



</example>

```ts [Palette.vue]
makeSortableList(list, {
  items: templates,
  group: { name: 'blocks', pull: 'clone', put: false },  // copies go out, nothing comes in
  sort: false,                                           // its own order stays
  clone: (block) => ({ ...block, id: crypto.randomUUID() }),
});
```

```ts [Sheet.vue]
makeSortableList(list, {
  items: blocks,
  group: 'blocks',
  clone: (block) => ({ ...block, id: crypto.randomUUID() }),  // for Alt-drags
  dropOutside: 'remove',                                      // drag off the Page panel to delete
});
```

- `pull: 'clone'` copies every drag out of the list. The original stays, and the copy
travels and lands.
- Holding <kbd value="Alt">



</kbd>

 while dragging copies too, from any list with a `clone`
function: it makes the copy. Change the key with the provider's `copyModifier`, or turn it
off with `null`.
- Either way, the list the item comes from needs `clone`. It must return the copy with a
**new key**. Without `clone`, nothing is copied.
- The drop event has `mode: 'copy'`, and `e.items` are the copies. An overlay component
gets `mode` too, to show a "+" while copying (see [the overlay](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/overlay)).

## Swap between lists

Two lists of one group that both have `behavior: 'swap'` exchange items between them: the
dragged item takes the hovered one's place, and the hovered one moves into the dragged
one's list. It must be allowed out of its list (`pull: true`) and into the other
(`put`). The on-call rotation in [sortable lists](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/sortable-lists#swap-instead-of-shift)
swaps across its two columns.

## Plain draggables

A list takes items dragged with `makeDraggable` (a chip, a template, a file from a tree)
when it has `createItem`. `group.put` decides on them too, with `from: null`. See
[plain draggables into a list](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/drag-and-drop#plain-draggables-into-a-list).

## Dropping outside

What happens when a drag ends over no target at all is the list's `dropOutside`:

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      <code>
        dropOutside
      </code>
    </th>
    
    <th>
      The items
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        'placeholder'
      </code>
      
       (default)
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Land where the slot was last shown.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        'cancel'
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Fly back. The default with <code>
        placeholder: 'indicator'
      </code>
      
      .
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        'remove'
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Leave their list: drag off to delete. The page of the palette demo does it.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`'remove'` asks the list's `onBeforeDrop` first. Then the list's `onDrop` runs with
`to.index === -1`, and `e.result` holds the list without the items. A trash can that takes
drops works the same way: see [trash zones](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/drag-and-drop#trash-zones).

## Controlled lists

The lists can read a store they don't own: Pinia, server state, immutable data. Pass
`items` as a getter (or a `computed`, or a readonly ref): the library never writes it.
Call `e.preventDefault()` in `onDrop` and apply `e.result` yourself:

<example height="26rem" hint="Move guests between the tables, then undo, one move at a time" name="seating-undo">



</example>

```ts [Table.vue]
const { items } = makeSortableList(list, {
  id: props.id,
  items: () => props.seating.state.tables[props.id]!,   // read-only
  group: 'seating',
  onDrop: (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();                                   // no write
    props.seating.apply(e.result, `${e.items[0]?.name} → ${props.title}`);
  },
});
```

```ts [store.ts]
const apply = (result: ReadonlyMap<Key, Guest[]>, label: string) => {
  const before = [...result.keys()].map((id): [Key, Guest[]] => [id, state.tables[id]!]);
  for (const [id, guests] of result) state.tables[id] = guests;
  state.history.unshift({ label, before });
};

const undo = () => {
  const last = state.history.shift();
  for (const [id, guests] of last?.before ?? []) state.tables[id] = guests;
};
```

- `e.result` maps every list the drop changes to its new array: both tables after a move,
one after a reorder. They are new arrays, so the store can keep the old ones for undo.
- The draft follows the store: apply `result` in `onDrop` (or before an async
`onBeforeDrop` resolves), and the overlay lands in the new order.
- `preventDefault()` skips the write into every list in `result`. Applied nowhere, the
lists stay as they were and the items fly back.
- Development builds warn when a read-only list's drop is left to the library: nothing
would change.

To save to a server before the drop lands, or to ask the user first, see
[drop decisions](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/drop-decisions). All list options are in the
[makeSortableList API](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/api/make-sortable-list).

- **Page:** Animations
- **Source:** https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/animations
- **Description:** Items slide while you sort, the drop lands on its slot, and data changes can animate too. Tune each one, animate the overlay, the slot and the lists with CSS, or bring motion or GSAP.

Three things animate on their own: the items sliding while you sort, the overlay landing on
drop, and, when you turn it on, the changes of your data that no drag made. Each one takes
the same values, on the provider or closer to what it animates:

Each takes `true` (the default timing), `false` (off), `{ duration, easing }`, or a function
that animates it yourself:

```vue
<DnDProvider
  :animation="{ duration: 180, easing: 'cubic-bezier(.2, .8, .2, 1)' }"
  :drop-animation="{ duration: 300 }"
  animate-changes
>
```

A list's or tree's own `animation` and `animateChanges` win over the provider's; for
`dropAnimation`, see [per item and per target](#per-item-and-per-target). The rest of the
motion is yours: the overlay, the slot and the lists are elements with
[data attributes and refs](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/styling), and CSS or an animation library moves them.

## Sorting

While you drag, the list's draft reorders and the items slide to their new places. The hand
below takes both options on its list: pick an `animation` and sort the cards, pick a
`dropAnimation` and let one go.

<example height="24rem" hint="Pick the timings, sort the cards, let one go off the table" name="anim-sort">



</example>

```ts [Hand.vue]
const springy: LayoutAnimation = ({ element, from, to, reducedMotion }) => {
  if (reducedMotion) return;
  return element.animate(
    [{ translate: `${from.left - to.left}px ${from.top - to.top}px` }, { translate: '0 0' }],
    { duration: 500, easing: 'cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1)' },
  );
};

const animation = shallowRef<LayoutAnimation>(true); // true, { duration: 600 }, springy or false
const dropAnimation = shallowRef<DropAnimation>(true); // true, { duration: 700 }, toss or false

const { items } = makeSortableList(table, {
  items: cards,
  strategy: 'horizontal',
  dropOutside: 'cancel', // let go off the table: the card flies back
  animation,
  dropAnimation,
});
```

It is FLIP on the CSS `translate` property, through the Web Animations API. `translate`
composes with any `transform` of yours, so a virtual list's row positioning stays intact.
When an item moves again before its animation ends, the next one starts from where it is
shown. The same animation moves the items on drop and on cancel.

The list's `animation` takes a value or a ref, read for every move: a ref switches it, as
above. A function there is an animation, not a getter.

<warning>

Don't wrap sortable items in `<TransitionGroup>`: every move would animate twice. For changes no
drag made, turn on [`animateChanges`](#data-changes-animatechanges).

</warning>

## The drop

On drop, the overlay flies from where you let go to the item's slot; on cancel, back to where
the item started. In the hand above, pick a `dropAnimation`, then drag a card off the table
and let go: the drop is cancelled, and it flies back. `toss` is a function of its own:

```ts [Hand.vue]
/** The overlay arcs to its slot, as if tossed. */
const toss: DropAnimation = ({ overlay, from, to, reducedMotion }) => {
  if (reducedMotion) return;
  // No visible slot to land on: fade out where it is.
  if (!to) return overlay.animate([{ opacity: 1 }, { opacity: 0 }], { duration: 200, fill: 'forwards' });
  const place = (x: number, y: number) => `translate3d(${x}px, ${y}px, 0)`;
  const rise = Math.min(120, Math.hypot(to.left - from.left, to.top - from.top) / 2);
  return overlay.animate(
    [
      { transform: place(from.left, from.top), width: `${from.width}px`, height: `${from.height}px` },
      { transform: place((from.left + to.left) / 2, Math.min(from.top, to.top) - rise), offset: 0.45 },
      { transform: place(to.left, to.top), width: `${to.width}px`, height: `${to.height}px` },
    ],
    { duration: 550, easing: 'ease-in-out', fill: 'forwards' },
  );
};
```

The hand gives it to its list. On the provider, it lands every drag:

```vue
<DnDProvider :drop-animation="toss">
```

- The box lands with its position (`transform`) and its size (`width`, `height`): the
content re-lays out at the slot's size, never scaled.
- When the item has no visible slot after the drop (scrolled away, or dropped into a folder
or a trash zone), `to` is `null`. The default then fades the overlay out, shrinking it into
the zone it was dropped on (`into`), or in place.
- In a multi-drag, the clones of the other items land on their own slots by themselves, with
the default timing when `dropAnimation` is a function. Into a zone, they go in one after
another, and the box after them (see [the files and folders](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/multi-drag#into-a-folder)).
- `dropAnimation` is read at every drop: a ref switches it for the next one, as in the hand,
and so does a provider prop bound to a ref.
- Scrolling while it lands doesn't send it astray. The box is `position: fixed`, so it
follows what it lands on (the slot, the zone, else the target it was dropped on) by its
CSS `translate`, on top of the `transform` the animation moves. Animate `transform` in
your own, as above, not `translate`.
- The next drag doesn't wait: each drop lands in a box of its own while new drags run. A
press on a landing box catches it in flight, and the drag goes on from where it is.
`onDragSettle` tells when a drag's overlay is home: the trash below shuts its lid then.

The overlay also takes the size of the slot it will land in while you drag
(`overlayFit: 'slot'`, the default), so a drop rarely needs a resize. See
[the overlay](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/overlay#size-overlayfit).

### Per item and per target

The provider's `dropAnimation` is the default. A draggable, a sortable item or a list (for
its items) can bring their own, and a drop target can have the last word on what lands in
it: `makeDroppable(el, { overDropAnimation })`, a list's or tree's `overDropAnimation`. For each
drop, the first one that is set:

1. The target's (none on a cancel).
2. The dragged item's own.
3. Its list's.
4. The provider's.

Below, the cart, the vase and the shelf each set one. The shelf lands its products with a
bounce, the vase has a slow landing of its own, and the cart takes what is dropped on it into
its icon: the product stays on its shelf, so its slot there is no place to land. Under the
shelf, the one each drag lands with lights up.

<example height="24rem" hint="Sort the mug, then the vase; then drop either into the cart" name="anim-cart">



</example>

```ts [Shop.vue]
// 3. The list's, for its items without one of their own.
makeSortableList(shelf, {
  items: products,
  strategy: 'horizontal',
  dropAnimation: { duration: 450, easing: 'cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1)' },
});
```

```ts [Product.vue]
// 2. The item's own: it wins over its list's.
makeSortableItem(el, {
  item: () => props.product,
  dropAnimation: props.product.fragile ? { duration: 1100, easing: 'ease-in-out' } : undefined,
});
```

```ts [Cart.vue]
// 1. The target's: it wins over both.
const intoCart: DropAnimation = ({ overlay, from, reducedMotion }) => {
  const end = icon.value?.getBoundingClientRect();
  if (!end || reducedMotion) return;
  // Into the icon, shrinking: the box scales around its top left corner.
  const scale = end.height / from.height;
  const animation = overlay.animate(
    [
      { transform: `translate3d(${from.left}px, ${from.top}px, 0)` },
      {
        transform: `translate3d(${end.left + (end.width - from.width * scale) / 2}px, ${end.top}px, 0) scale(${scale})`,
        opacity: 0,
      },
    ],
    { duration: 450, easing: 'cubic-bezier(.55, 0, .75, .2)', fill: 'forwards' },
  );
  animation.finished.then(() => landed.value++, () => {}); // the icon bounces
  return animation;
};

makeDroppable(el, { id: 'cart', overDropAnimation: intoCart, onDrop: … });
```

`false` counts as set: a target with `overDropAnimation: false` keeps the overlay where it was
dropped. The function gets the target as `over`, so one function can treat targets apart.

### The content's own landing

The drop also waits for the animations inside the overlay that are running when it starts:
CSS animations and transitions an overlay component starts on `status: 'dropping'`. Over
the trash, a photo crumples up; dropped, it is thrown into the bin, and the drop ends when
it is in:

<example height="27rem" hint="Drag a photo into the trash; Undo brings it back" name="anim-trash">



</example>

```ts [TrashBin.vue]
makeDroppable(el, {
  id: 'trash',
  // The overlay reads it as `over.data`: it aims the photo at the bin's mouth.
  data: () => ({ bin: bin.value }),
  overOverlay: Crumple,
  // The box stays where it was let go: its content does the landing.
  overDropAnimation: false,
  onDrop: (event) => emit('drop', event), // the gallery calls `event.source?.remove()`
});

// Its landing is over: the photo is in, the lid shuts.
useDnDMonitor({
  onDragSettle: (event) => {
    if ('dropped' in event && event.over?.id === 'trash') shut.value++;
  },
});
```

```vue [Crumple.vue]
<template>
  <div class="crumple">
    <!-- `fall` is set at the drop: `--dx` and `--dy`, from the photo to the bin in `over.data`. -->
    <div class="paper" :class="{ falling: fall }" :style="fall">
      <slot />
    </div>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.paper { clip-path: polygon(…); rotate: -8deg; scale: 0.7; }
.paper.falling { animation: fall 0.55s forwards; }
@keyframes fall {
  to { translate: var(--dx) var(--dy); rotate: -120deg; scale: 0.12; opacity: 0; }
}
</style>
```

Finished animations and endless loops don't count, and the drop waits two seconds at most.

## Data changes: `animateChanges`

Drag a tile, then shuffle, add and remove some. The drag animates by default; the buttons'
changes animate because the grid turns on `animateChanges`.

<example height="22.75rem" hint="Drag, shuffle, add, remove" name="animate">



</example>

```ts
makeSortableList(listRef, { items: swatches, animateChanges: true });
```

Off by default, `animateChanges` animates what changes your array without a drag: a sort, a shuffle, a
move between lists of one group, an item added, removed or filtered out. In a tree it also covers
the rows a node shows or hides as it expands and collapses. `<DnDProvider animate-changes>` turns it on for
every list and tree.

Its parts can be tuned one by one:

```ts
animateChanges: { duration: 250, move: true, enter: true, leave: { duration: 150 } },
```

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Part
    </th>
    
    <th>
      By default
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        move
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Items that changed places slide, as with <code>
        animation
      </code>
      
      .
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        enter
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Items that appeared fade in where they are.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        leave
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      A copy of the item that left fades out where it was, shrinking a little. It is marked <code>
        data-dnd-leaving
      </code>
      
       and removed when it's done.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`duration` and `easing` apply to every part; each part takes `true`, options, `false` or a
function. Only items near the visible area animate, so rows a virtual list hasn't mounted are
skipped. The option is read when `items` changes, so a ref can switch it, as the demo's toggle
does.

## The overlay: lift, tilt, settle

The overlay box says what it is doing: `data-dnd-overlay="dragging"` while it follows the
pointer, `"dropping"` while it lands. The library moves and sizes the box. Inside it,
`data-dnd-overlay-content` holds all the overlay shows, one clone or a whole stack, and is
yours to animate. Pick a candidate up: the overlay lifts and tilts; let go: it lies flat as
it lands.

<example height="24.5rem" hint="Pick a candidate up, drag it to Hired, let go" name="anim-container">



</example>

```vue [index.vue]
<template>
  <DnDProvider overlay-class="pipeline-hand">…</DnDProvider>
</template>

<!-- Not scoped: the overlay's content element is the library's, outside this component. -->
<style>
.pipeline-hand {
  transition:
    rotate 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1),
    scale 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1);
}

[data-dnd-overlay='dragging'] > .pipeline-hand {
  rotate: 3deg;
  scale: 1.05;
}

/* Where the lift starts: the box appears already `dragging`. */
@starting-style {
  [data-dnd-overlay='dragging'] > .pipeline-hand {
    rotate: 0deg;
    scale: 1;
  }
}
</style>
```

- `overlay-class` puts your classes on the overlay content of this provider: the drag's and
the ones still landing. Tailwind takes it too (`starting:` writes `@starting-style`).
- A transition needs a start, and the box appears already `dragging`: `@starting-style`
gives the lift its "before". When the box turns `dropping`, the transition runs back, and
the drop waits for it to end.
- The content itself animates the same way, in its own component: the
[board](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/examples/board)'s card in hand and its columns tilt as they are picked up
(`[data-dnd-overlay='dragging'] .column` with `@starting-style`). Keyframes work too: they
play from the start of the state.
- An **overlay component** gets `status` as a prop: its transitions can follow it. The note of
[the provider's slot demo](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/overlay#the-providers-overlay-slot) straightens with
`transition: rotate 0.25s` when `status` turns `'dropping'`.
- Leave the box itself (`[data-dnd-overlay]`) alone: a transition on it would lag behind the
pointer, and the library writes its `transform` and size.

## The slot and the lists

The dragged element stays in its list as the **slot** it will land in, marked
`data-dnd-placeholder`. Its lists know about the drag too: `isAccepting` while a drag runs
that they take, `isOver` while it is over them. In the pipeline above, every lane gets ready
as you pick a candidate up, the one under the card lights up, its count bumps, and the slot
opens and breathes.

```vue [Lane.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
const { items, isOver, isAccepting } = makeSortableList(list, {
  id: props.lane.id,
  items: toRef(props.lane, 'people'),
  group: 'pipeline',
  dropzone: zone,
});
</script>

<template>
  <section ref="zone" class="lane" :class="{ ready: isAccepting, over: isOver }">
    <h3>
      {{ lane.title }}
      <!-- A new element for every count: its animation plays on each change. -->
      <span :key="items.length" class="count">{{ items.length }}</span>
    </h3>
    <ul ref="list">…</ul>
  </section>
</template>

<style scoped>
.lane { transition: background-color 0.25s, box-shadow 0.25s; }
.lane.ready { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, #42b883 35%, transparent); }
.lane.over { background: color-mix(in srgb, #42b883 8%, transparent); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px #42b883; }
.count { animation: bump 0.3s ease-out; }
</style>
```

```css [Candidate.vue]
/* The slot opens where it appears, then breathes until the card lands. */
.candidate[data-dnd-placeholder] {
  animation: open 0.2s ease-out, breathe 1.2s ease-in-out 0.2s infinite;
}
```

- `items` is the draft: its `length` counts the card as soon as its slot enters the lane, so
the count changes while you drag.
- A slot that moves to another list is a new element there, so its keyframes play again.
- The lists themselves grow and shrink smoothly as a slot comes in and leaves, and so does
what is around them (`animateSize`, on by default; `false` lets them jump). Leave their
sizes to that: a list you resize while a drag runs moves the targets under the pointer.
Glows, outlines, colors and `scale` are safe.

## Your own animations

Each option also takes a function. It gets a context, starts the animation and returns its
`Animation`, a promise that settles when it ends, or nothing. The drag ends when the drop
animation does, and a leaving copy is removed when its animation does, but neither waits more
than a second past `options.duration` (250 ms for the drop, 200 ms for the others).

```ts
// animation, animateChanges.move: an item moved from `from` to `to`
({ key, element, from, to, options, reason, signal, reducedMotion }) => Animation | Promise | void
// dropAnimation: `to` is null when there is no visible slot; `into` is the zone it went into
({ overlay, from, to, into, reason, active, options, reducedMotion }) => …
// animateChanges.enter: the element is already in place
({ key, element, to, options, reducedMotion }) => …
// animateChanges.leave: `element` is a copy where the item was, removed when you finish
({ key, element, from, options, reducedMotion }) => …
```

`reason` says why: `'drag'` or `'change'` for a move, `'drop'` or `'cancel'` for the
overlay. `options` holds the timing of the option, so a function can follow the
`duration` you set next to it.

Three rules keep custom animations in step with the library:

- **Animate translate** from `from - to` to zero, not `transform`. It composes with transforms
that virtual lists or your CSS put on rows, and drags measure items without it.
- **Honor signal.** It aborts when the item moves again before the animation ends. Stop your
animation and clear its styles at once: the layout is measured right after. A returned
`Animation` is cancelled for you.
- **Land on a slot with position and size** (`width`, `height`), not `scale`: the overlay's
content re-lays out at the slot's size. Where there is no slot to land on, shrinking is
fine: the default scales the overlay down into the zone (`into`), and the cart above into
its icon.

### motion

The garland below runs on [motion](https://motion.dev/docs/vue): the flags and the drop
spring through the provider's functions, and the overlay component swings with the
pointer's speed.

<example height="17rem" hint="Drag a flag fast from side to side, then let go" name="anim-motion">



</example>

```vue [index.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { animate } from 'motion-v';
import { DnDProvider, type DropAnimationContext, type LayoutAnimationContext } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const spring = { type: 'spring', duration: 0.5, bounce: 0.3 } as const;

const move = ({ element, from, to, signal, reducedMotion }: LayoutAnimationContext) => {
  if (reducedMotion) return;
  const controls = animate(element, { translate: [`${from.left - to.left}px ${from.top - to.top}px`, '0px 0px'] }, spring);
  signal.addEventListener('abort', () => {
    controls.stop();
    element.style.translate = '';
  });
  return controls.finished;
};

const drop = ({ overlay, from, to, reducedMotion }: DropAnimationContext) => {
  if (reducedMotion) return;
  if (!to) return animate(overlay, { opacity: 0 }, { duration: 0.18 }).finished;
  return animate(
    overlay,
    { x: [from.left, to.left], y: [from.top, to.top], width: [from.width, to.width], height: [from.height, to.height] },
    spring,
  ).finished;
};
</script>

<template>
  <DnDProvider :animation="move" :drop-animation="drop">
    <Garland />
  </DnDProvider>
</template>
```

The overlay component renders under the provider, so `useDnD()` works in it. It follows the
pointer through a motion value:

```vue [FlagOverlay.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { motion, useMotionValue, useReducedMotion, useSpring, useTransform, useVelocity } from 'motion-v';
import { useDnD, type DnDStatus, type DragItem } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const props = defineProps<{ items: DragItem[]; status: DnDStatus }>();

const { pointer } = useDnD();
const x = useMotionValue(pointer.value?.x ?? 0);
watch(() => pointer.value?.x, (value) => value !== undefined && x.set(value));
const swing = useSpring(useTransform(useVelocity(x), [-1500, 0, 1500], [-25, 0, 25]), { stiffness: 300, damping: 14 });
const calm = useReducedMotion();
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Held by its top edge: `transform-origin: 50% 0` in its CSS. -->
  <motion.div
    class="flag-overlay"
    :style="{ rotate: calm ? 0 : swing }"
    :animate="{ scale: status === 'dropping' || calm ? 1 : 1.1 }"
  >
    …
  </motion.div>
</template>
```

### GSAP

```ts [gsap-animations.ts]
import gsap from 'gsap';
import type {
  DropAnimationContext,
  EnterAnimationContext,
  LayoutAnimationContext,
  LeaveAnimationContext,
  Rect,
} from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const move = ({ element, from, to, signal, reducedMotion }: LayoutAnimationContext) => {
  if (reducedMotion) return;
  const tween = gsap.fromTo(
    element,
    { translate: `${from.left - to.left}px ${from.top - to.top}px` },
    { translate: '0px 0px', duration: 0.4, ease: 'power3.out' },
  );
  signal.addEventListener('abort', () => tween.revert());
  return tween.then();
};

const box = (rect: Rect) => ({ x: rect.left, y: rect.top, width: rect.width, height: rect.height });

const drop = ({ overlay, from, to, reducedMotion }: DropAnimationContext) => {
  if (reducedMotion) return;
  if (!to) return gsap.to(overlay, { opacity: 0, duration: 0.2 }).then();
  return gsap.fromTo(overlay, box(from), { ...box(to), duration: 0.45, ease: 'back.out(1.2)' }).then();
};

const enter = ({ element, reducedMotion }: EnterAnimationContext) =>
  gsap.from(element, reducedMotion ? { opacity: 0, duration: 0.2 } : { opacity: 0, scale: 0.85, duration: 0.35 }).then();

const leave = ({ element, reducedMotion }: LeaveAnimationContext) =>
  gsap.to(element, reducedMotion ? { opacity: 0, duration: 0.2 } : { opacity: 0, scale: 0.85, duration: 0.25 }).then();

export const gsapAnimations = { animation: move, dropAnimation: drop, animateChanges: { move, enter, leave } };
```

```vue
<DnDProvider v-bind="gsapAnimations">
```

The full option types are in [Animations](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/api/animations).

## Reduced motion

With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the library's own animations don't run: items and the
overlay go straight to their places, and the overlay doesn't glide between slot sizes. Your
functions always run, with `reducedMotion: true`, so they decide: skip the motion, or keep a
short fade, as the recipes above do.

Your CSS is yours to guard. Put lifts, tilts and pulses in
`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, as the demos on this page do, and keep
the color changes outside it: they tell where a drop goes.

## Layout changes the library didn't cause

When something else moves rows during a drag — a virtualizer re-measuring, an image loading —
call the list's `captureLayout()` right before the change renders. It measures the rows where they
are and animates them to their new places after the next render. Outside a drag it does nothing.
See [Virtual lists](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/virtual-lists).

---

- **Page:** Drag and drop
- **Source:** https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/drag-and-drop
- **Description:** Free dragging with makeDraggable and drop targets with makeDroppable — typed targets that take some drags and refuse others, a floor plan, trash zones, folders inside a list, and plain items a list takes in.

Use `makeDraggable` and `makeDroppable` for anything that isn't a sortable list: waste
into bins, furniture on a floor plan, files into folders, a trash can, a chess board.

<example height="29rem" hint="Sort the waste into the bins; no bin takes the battery" name="recycling">



</example>

## A draggable

```vue [WasteItem.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeDraggable } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const props = defineProps<{ waste: { id: string; name: string; type: string } }>();
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');

const { isDragging } = makeDraggable(el, {
  id: () => props.waste.id,      // read back as `active.id`
  type: () => props.waste.type,  // matched by the targets' `accept`
  data: () => props.waste,       // anything: `active.data`
});
</script>

<template>
  <div ref="el" :class="{ dragging: isDragging }">{{ waste.name }}</div>
</template>
```

Pass the id from your data, as a getter. The default id comes from `useId()` and is new
for every component instance, so it means nothing to the rest of your app. Options are read
when they are needed, so a getter or a ref keeps them current.

Buttons, inputs and other interactive children don't start a pointer drag, so they keep

## A drop target

```vue [Bin.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeDroppable, type Key } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';
import type { Bin, Waste } from './waste';

const props = defineProps<{ bin: Bin; items: Waste[] }>();
const emit = defineEmits<{ drop: [id: Key] }>();
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');

const { isOver, isAccepting } = makeDroppable(el, {
  id: props.bin.id,
  accept: props.bin.accept,   // 'glass', ['paper', 'cardboard'], a function…
  onDrop: (event) => emit('drop', event.active.id),
});
</script>

<template>
  <section ref="el" :class="{ accepting: isAccepting, over: isOver && isAccepting, refused: isOver && !isAccepting }">
    <WasteItem v-for="waste in items" :key="waste.id" :waste="waste" />
  </section>
</template>
```

## Which drags a target takes

A draggable's `type` is matched against a target's `accept`:

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      <code>
        accept
      </code>
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Takes
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      omitted or <code>
        '*'
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Everything.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        'glass'
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Draggables of type <code>
        glass
      </code>
      
      , and untyped ones.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        ['paper', 'cardboard']
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Either type, and untyped ones.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        ({ active, items, types }) => boolean
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Whatever your function says.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A draggable without a `type` fits any string rule. `type` can be an array too
(`['paper', 'large']`): one matching type is enough. A function decides on anything about
the drag. The compost bin above reads the items' data, not their type:

```ts [waste.ts]
{
  id: 'compost',
  accept: ({ items }) => items.every((item) => (item.data as Waste).compostable),
}
```

`accept` is read live, while the drag looks for its target: pass a ref to change it.

When several items are dragged at once, `acceptMode` says how many must fit: `'all'`
(default) or `'some'`. With `'some'`, return the ids to keep from `onBeforeDrop`, and the
others fly back. See [drop decisions](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/drop-decisions).

## The drop

`onDrop` of a plain drop target is where **you** change your data. The library moves
nothing on its own:

```vue [index.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
/** Where each item is: the tray or a bin. */
const place = reactive<Record<string, string>>(Object.fromEntries(WASTE.map((waste) => [waste.id, 'tray'])));
const itemsIn = (bin: string) => WASTE.filter((waste) => place[waste.id] === bin);
const drop = (bin: string, id: Key) => (place[String(id)] = bin);
</script>

<template>
  <Bin v-for="bin in BINS" :key="bin.id" :bin="bin" :items="itemsIn(bin.id)" @drop="drop(bin.id, $event)" />
</template>
```

`active.ids` holds every dragged id, the grabbed one first. The order is `onBeforeDrop`
(decide), `onDrop` (apply), then the provider's `drag-end`. To hear every drag of the
page in one place, use `useDnDMonitor` (see [the provider](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/provider)). To
ask before a drop, keep the drag going, or accept only some items, see
[drop decisions](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/drop-decisions).

## Leave it where it was dropped

A floor plan, a canvas, a board: the item stays where you let go. Every event carries
`position`, the `left` / `top` that put an absolutely positioned item where it was
dropped.

<example height="28rem" hint="Drag furniture into the room, move it around, or put it back" name="room-planner">



</example>

```ts [Planner.vue]
const room = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('room');
makeDroppable(room, {
  id: 'room',
  onDrop: ({ active, position }) => {
    const piece = find(active.id);
    if (!piece || !position || !room.value) return;
    // Clamped, so a piece let go half outside stays inside the walls.
    piece.x = clamp(position.x, room.value.clientWidth - piece.width);
    piece.y = clamp(position.y, room.value.clientHeight - piece.height);
    piece.place = 'room';
  },
});
```

```vue [Piece.vue]
<div ref="el" class="piece" :style="{ left: `${piece.x}px`, top: `${piece.y}px` }">…</div>
```

`position` is the top-left corner of the dragged box in `over`, measured from its padding
edge, with its scroll added: the room's border, its walls, doesn't count. It is `null`
over nothing.

<tip>

Don't compute the spot from `active.rect` and `delta`: that misses the target's border
and scroll. Grids, bounds and axis locks for such boards are in
[constraints](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/constraints).

</tip>

## Without an overlay

By default a copy of the element follows the pointer, and the element stays in place: the
furniture in storage works that way. With `overlay: false` there is no copy, and the
element moves itself by the `transform` the drag returns: the furniture in the room.

```ts [Piece.vue]
const inRoom = computed(() => props.piece.place === 'room');
const { isDragging, transform } = makeDraggable(el, {
  id: () => props.piece.id,
  overlay: computed(() => !inRoom.value),   // a value or a ref, read when the drag starts
});

const style = computed(() => ({
  left: `${props.piece.x}px`,
  top: `${props.piece.y}px`,
  ...(transform.value && { transform: `translate3d(${transform.value.x}px, ${transform.value.y}px, 0)` }),
}));
```

- `position` is then the element's own corner, so the drop handler stays the same.
- The element is under the pointer while it moves; finding the target, the library looks
through it. Raise it above its neighbours while it is dragged (`z-index`).
- It scrolls with the page, the overlay doesn't: `transform` takes off what its container
moved since the drag started, so it stays under the pointer when the page scrolls.
- It moves inside its own container: an `overflow: hidden` parent clips it, and its
stacking context decides what it passes over. The overlay has neither problem.

For a custom preview instead of the copy, see [the overlay](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/overlay).

## Trash zones

A drag that starts in a sortable list carries `e.source`. Call `remove()` and the list
drops the items:

<example height="34rem" hint="Drag a notification to Done or Delete, then undo" name="triage">



</example>

```ts [Triage.vue]
const triage = (bin: 'done' | 'deleted') => (e: DnDEvent) => {
  bins[bin].push(...e.active.items.map((entry) => entry.item as Notice));
  e.source?.remove();
};

makeDroppable(doneZone, { id: 'done', onDrop: triage('done') });
makeDroppable(trashZone, { id: 'trash', onDrop: triage('deleted') });
```

- `e.active.items[i].item` is the list's item itself. Keep it, and an undo puts it back
where it was.
- The list's own `onDrop` then runs with `to.index === -1`, and `e.result` holds the list
without the items.
- The overlay shrinks into the zone, as the item is no longer shown anywhere.
- A list can also remove what is dropped outside of everything: see
[`dropOutside`](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/shared-lists#dropping-outside).

<note>

With the keyboard, the arrows move a list's item between the slots of its list and the
lists of its group; past the end of the lists, the next press carries it on to the drop
target that way, here the trash, and the opposite arrow brings it back. A button, a menu or
the `Delete` key is still quicker for many people: offer one too.

</note>

## Drop into a sortable item

A row of a sortable list can be a drop target too: a folder that takes bookmarks, a group
that takes tasks. Put a droppable on the item's element:

<example height="28rem" hint="Drop a link on the middle of a folder; near its edges it sorts. Open a folder to drag links out" name="bookmarks">



</example>

```ts [FolderRow.vue]
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');
makeSortableItem(el, { item: () => props.folder, type: 'folder' });

const { isOver } = makeDroppable(el, {
  accept: 'link',
  onDrop: (e) => {
    emit('add', e.active.items.map((entry) => entry.item as Link)); // Bookmarks adds them
    e.source?.remove();   // take them out of the list they came from
  },
});
```

An open folder shows its links as a list of the same group, which takes links only: they
sort there, and drag back out to the top level or into another folder.

While the list would sort the drag, such a target counts only in the **middle** of its
item (25 to 75% along the list's axis). There the drop goes into the item, and the list
doesn't move. Near the edges, the list sorts as usual.

- A target whose `accept` refuses the drag is skipped: the list sorts over the item as
over any other. The folders take only links, so a dragged folder sorts past the others.
- A target never receives its own drag.
- With the keyboard, an arrow stops on the folder first; the next press in the same
direction goes on past it.
- The item is no longer shown after the drop, so the overlay shrinks into the folder
instead of flying back.
- Over the folder the list keeps the dragged row's slot where it was, so nothing shifts
under the pointer. The slot gets `data-dnd-placeholder="into"` then: the drop doesn't go
there, so hide it if you like (`[data-dnd-placeholder='into'] { opacity: 0 }`).

The [file manager](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/examples/file-manager) does the same in a grid, with nested
folders.

## Plain draggables into a list

A sortable list takes in items dragged with `makeDraggable` when it knows how to make an
item from them:

<example height="26rem" hint="Drag a block into the agenda; the times follow the drag" name="day-planner">



</example>

```ts [Agenda.vue]
const { items } = makeSortableList(list, {
  items: agenda,
  createItem: (active) => ({ ...(active.data as Block), id: `entry-${++created}` }),
});
```

While the draggable is over the list, the created item sits in the draft and is rendered
by your template like any other row: the agenda's times already count it. It becomes real
on drop (`mode: 'insert'`, `from.list === null`), and the overlay lands on it.

- Return `undefined` to refuse. Lists without `createItem` ignore plain draggables.
- Give the new item a key of its own: the block stays in the palette.
- With the keyboard, an arrow toward the list takes the draggable in, level with it, and
the next arrows move it by slots.

## Files from the computer

Files dragged in from the desktop or a file manager aren't the library's drags: the browser
carries them. A drop target takes them with `external`, and the drop brings them in
`e.external`:

<example height="22rem" hint="Drag image or PDF files from your computer onto the zones" name="file-drop">



</example>

```ts [AvatarDrop.vue]
const { isOver, isAccepting } = makeDroppable(el, {
  external: { files: 'image/*', multiple: false },
  onDrop: (e) => show(e.external!.files[0]!),
});
```

- `files` reads like `<input accept>`: MIME types (`image/*`, `application/pdf`) and
extensions (`.md`). `true` takes any file, a function decides file by file. `links` and
`text` take what other apps and tabs drag, `types` any other MIME type.
- The drag runs as a drag of the provider: `isOver`, `isAccepting`, the events and the
announcements work as for any other. Targets without `external` ignore it. There is no
overlay: the browser draws the dragged image.
- While the files are held over the page, the browser tells their types only
(`e.external.fileTypes`). Their names, sizes and contents come with the drop, and
extensions are checked then. Folders are left out; with `multiple: false`, a drag of
several files is refused.

Lists take files, links and text too, and make room for them while they are held. Items can
also leave the page, into another app or another window of yours: see
[files and other apps](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/native).

<tip>

Keyboard and screen reader users can't drag files. Offer an `<input type="file">` next to
the zone, as the demo does with Browse.

</tip>

## Step by step

<steps level="3">

### Wrap the app in a provider

`DnDProvider` owns the drag. Every composable must run in a component **rendered inside** it —
not in the component whose template contains it.

### Make a list

`makeSortableList` takes the list's element and your array. It returns `items`: a draft that
reorders live while you drag. Render the draft, not your array, and key the rows by id.

### Make the rows

Each row calls `makeSortableItem` with its element and the item it renders. Its key comes from
`item.id`.

</steps>

When the drop lands, `tasks` gets the new order — it's a regular `ref`, so the rest of your app
sees the change like any other.

<tip>

Using Pinia, a server or immutable data? Pass a getter instead of a ref, then call
`e.preventDefault()` in `onDrop` and apply `e.result` yourself.

</tip>

---

- **Page:** The provider
- **Source:** https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/provider
- **Description:** DnDProvider owns every drag under it. It finds the target, starts drags, scrolls, and tells useDnD and useDnDMonitor everything that happens.

## One provider for the app

```vue [App.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { DnDProvider } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';
</script>

<template>
  <DnDProvider>
    <RouterView />
  </DnDProvider>
</template>
```

Put one `DnDProvider` high up, in `App.vue` or a layout, and forget about it. Every
composable (`makeSortableList`, `makeDraggable`, `useDnD`…) looks for the closest provider
above the component it runs in.

<warning>

A composable must run in a component **rendered inside** the provider. Calling it in the
component whose own template contains `<DnDProvider>` throws
`No <DnDProvider> found above this component`: Vue's `inject` only sees ancestors.

</warning>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      Input
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Turns pointer, touch and keyboard input into drags (<code>
        sensors
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        activation
      </code>
      
      ), one drag at a time.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Finding the target
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Hit-tests the drop targets under the drag (<code>
        collision
      </code>
      
      ) and tells them.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      The overlay
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Renders the box that follows the pointer, teleported to <code>
        body
      </code>
      
      , and lands it on drop.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      The selection
    </td>
    
    <td>
      One set of selected ids, shared by every list and draggable under it.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      Auto-scroll
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Scrolls containers and the window when a drag nears their edges.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      The live region
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Announces pickups, moves, drops and cancels to screen readers.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

It renders nothing else: your markup stays as it is.

## Read the drag: `useDnD()`

<example height="27rem" hint="Drag a task and watch the state" name="provider-state">

import { useDnD } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

```vue [DropHint.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue';
import { useDnD } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const { status, over } = useDnD();
const refused = computed(() => status.value === 'dragging' && over.value?.accepted === false);
</script>

<template>
  <p v-if="refused" role="status">This list doesn't take that.</p>
</template>
```

As soon as a drop is decided, `active`, `over` and `pointer` read `null`, even while the
overlay is still landing (`status` reads `'dropping'`). UI derived from them never shows
the old drag next to the new data. While an async `onBeforeDrop` waits, the state stays as
it was at release.

The next drag doesn't wait for a landing: it starts at once, and `status` reads
`'dragging'` while the last overlay lands around it. A press on a landing overlay catches
it in flight: the drag goes on from where the overlay is. `onDragSettle` tells when a drag's
overlay is home.

## Listen to every drag: `useDnDMonitor()`

```ts
import { useDnDMonitor } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

useDnDMonitor({
  onDragStart: ({ active }) => {},
  onDragMove: ({ pointer, delta }) => {},
  onDragOver: ({ over }) => {},                  // the target changed
  onBeforeDrop: (e) => 'accept',                 // or 'reject', 'continue', some ids; may be async
  onDragEnd: ({ active, over, dropped, accepted, position }) => {},
  onDragCancel: ({ active }) => {},
  onDragResume: ({ active }) => {},              // onBeforeDrop answered 'continue'
  onDragSettle: ({ active, over }) => {},        // its overlay has landed
});
```

A monitor hears every drag under its provider, wherever it starts: the panel above logs
the list's drags without importing it. It stops when the component that called it
unmounts.

Every event carries `active`, `over`, `pointer`, `delta` (the offset from the start),
`position` (where the dragged box sits in `over`, see
[drag and drop](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/drag-and-drop#leave-it-where-it-was-dropped)) and, for items
from a sortable list, `source`. The full shapes are in the [events API](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/api/events).

<note>

`onDragEnd` is the place for "after the drop" work: saving, clearing the selection,
analytics. A list's own `onDrop` runs **before** its write, so it still sees the old order.

</note>

## Finding the target

Pick a function, then drag the pin or the card over the targets. The badges show how the
function ranks them on this frame; the green one is the target.

<example height="33rem" hint="Switch the function, drag over the nested, small and overlapping targets" name="collision-lab">



</example>

On every frame of a drag, the provider gives `collision` the drop targets in play, and it
returns their ids, best first. Five functions come with the library:

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Function
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Ranks
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Good for
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        pointerFirst
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      What is under the pointer; when that's nothing, what the dragged box overlaps.
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The default: precise under the pointer, forgiving in the gaps.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        pointerWithin
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Only what is under the pointer, the innermost first.
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Precise targets: a gap drops nowhere.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        rectIntersection
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Every target the dragged box overlaps: higher <code>
        priority
      </code>
      
      , then deeper nesting, then the bigger overlap.
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Big items over small targets, where the pointer is at the item's edge.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        closestCenter
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Every target, by the distance from the box's center to theirs.
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Something always wins, even far away: grids and lists of same-size items.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        closestCorners
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Every target, by the distances between the four corners.
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Columns stacked side by side (kanban), targets of very different heights.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Under the pointer, hit-testing respects what the user sees: of overlapping targets only the
one on top is hit (`front`, never `back` where they overlap), and of nested ones the
innermost comes first (`subfolder`, then `folder`).

### A function of your own

```ts [magnet.ts]
import type { CollisionDetection, Coordinates, Rect } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

/** How far the point is from the rect: 0 inside it. */
const gap = (rect: Rect, point: Coordinates) =>
  Math.hypot(
    Math.max(rect.left - point.x, 0, point.x - rect.right),
    Math.max(rect.top - point.y, 0, point.y - rect.bottom),
  );

/** What is under the pointer; in a gap, the nearest target within 40px. */
export const magnet: CollisionDetection = ({ hits, pointer, candidates }) => {
  if (hits.length) return hits;
  return candidates
    .filter((candidate) => gap(candidate.rect, pointer) <= 40)
    .sort((a, b) => gap(a.rect, pointer) - gap(b.rect, pointer))
    .map((candidate) => candidate.id);
};
```

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Argument
    </th>
    
    <th>
      What it holds
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        pointer
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The pointer, after modifiers.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        overlayRect
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The dragged box as it is shown, <code>
        null
      </code>
      
       without an overlay.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        candidates
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Every target in play: <code>
        id
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        rect
      </code>
      
       (its visible part, clipped by scroll containers), <code>
        priority
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        depth
      </code>
      
       (<code>
        0
      </code>
      
       at the top, deeper when nested).
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        hits
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The targets under the pointer, from hit-testing, best first.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Return an empty array for "no target". Disabled targets, targets inside the dragged items
and targets hidden by their scroll containers never reach the function. A target that
refuses the drag still competes: over it, `over.accepted` is `false` and a drop is refused
(a target inside a sortable item steps aside instead, so the list sorts over it). The demo
wraps the chosen function to record its ranking:
`(args) => (ranked.value = detect(args))`.

<note>

The provider damps the switches the function asks for. A target the drag just left can't
win again until the pointer has moved 10 px, so boundaries don't flicker. Between the
targets nested in a parent (the gaps of a column of cards), the last target stays.

</note>

## When a press becomes a drag

A press doesn't drag at once. `activation` sets, per pointer kind (`mouse`, `touch`,
`pen`), what it waits for: a `distance` in px, a `delay` in ms (with a `tolerance` past
which the press gives up, so the page can scroll), or whichever of the two comes first.

```vue
<DnDProvider :activation="{ mouse: { distance: 8 }, touch: { delay: 300, tolerance: 8 } }">
```

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Pointer
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Default
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        mouse
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        pen
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        { distance: 4 }
      </code>
      
      : a click stays a click. A mouse press on a <code>
        handle
      </code>
      
       starts at once, and is still a click if it doesn't move.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        touch
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        { delay: 200, tolerance: 5 }
      </code>
      
      : a long press, so lists keep scrolling under a finger.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A kind you leave out keeps its default. A draggable's own `activation` wins over a
[drag area's](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/constraints), which wins over the provider's. While a press
waits, `useDnD().status` is `'activating'` and `activation.progress` runs from `0` to `1`;
Escape or `useDnD().cancel()` gives it up. Try the constraints live, and draw a long-press
ring from the progress, in [sensors](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/sensors#activation-constraints).

## Auto-scroll

Drag a channel toward the top or the bottom of the list. The green bands are the edge
zones: the deeper into one, the faster the list scrolls.

<example height="37.5rem" hint="Drag a channel into the green bands" name="auto-scroll-edges">



</example>

Any element with `overflow: auto` or `scroll` scrolls by itself, and so does the window. The
provider scrolls the container under the pointer first, then its ancestors, then the
window.

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Option
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Default
    </th>
    
    <th>
      What it sets
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        threshold
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        0.2
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The edge zone, as a fraction of the container's size, between 24 and 96 px.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        acceleration
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        10
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The speed at the very edge, in px per frame. It grows with the square of the depth into the zone, so the start is slow and precise.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        maxSpeed
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        25
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The top speed. Past the edge (the pointer outside the container), the speed keeps growing up to it.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`:auto-scroll="false"` turns it off. A direction scrolls only once the pointer has moved
that way, so an item picked up near an edge doesn't scroll by itself. Lists, trees and
[drag areas](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/constraints) take an `autoScroll` of their own for their
container:

```ts
makeSortableList(list, { items: channels, autoScroll: { maxSpeed: 10 } });
```

Keyboard drags never auto-scroll: they scroll the item into view instead. `isAutoScrolling`
(from `useDnD()`, or a drag area) is `true` while something scrolls.

## Haptics and the copy key

A touch drag vibrates briefly when it starts. `:haptics="false"` turns that off; an object
sets each vibration:

```vue
<DnDProvider :haptics="{ start: true, enter: 10, drop: 10, refuse: [20, 40, 20] }">
```

Each takes `true` (the default pattern), a length in ms, an on/off pattern, or `false`.
Only drags started by touch vibrate, and iOS Safari can't vibrate at all.

`copyModifier` is the key that, held during a drag between lists, turns the move into a
copy: `'Alt'` by default, any `KeyboardEvent.key`, or `null` for none. The list the items
come from needs a `clone` function; see [lists that share items](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/shared-lists).

## Several providers

Most apps need exactly one. Put the wishlist under its own provider, then try to move a book
across: it can't leave its provider, and the outer monitor stops hearing the wishlist.

<example height="33.5rem" hint="Move a book across, then give the wishlist its own provider" name="provider-nested">



</example>

```vue
<DnDProvider>
  <Shelf v-model="reading" />
  <DnDProvider>
    <Shelf v-model="wishlist" />
    <EventLog />            <!-- hears the inner provider's drags only -->
  </DnDProvider>
</DnDProvider>
```

- Providers are independent: a drag never crosses from one to another.
- Nested providers are allowed. The **closest owner wins**: an item belongs to the nearest
provider above it, and the outer provider ignores it.
- Each provider has its own selection, overlay, live region and monitors.

A second provider makes sense only for a part of the page that needs its own provider-wide
settings (collision, keyboard keys, announcements) and whose items never leave it. If
items can't move between two parts of your page, check that they don't sit under two
providers.

<tip>

Rules for one part of the page (a board that snaps, a feed with a longer touch press, a
panel where nothing drags) don't need a provider of their own:

```ts
makeDragArea(board, { modifiers: [snapToGrid(20)], activation: { touch: { delay: 400 } } });
```

Its items stay in the app's provider and can still move anywhere. See
[constraints](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/constraints).

</tip>

An app mounted elsewhere, inside a shadow root or as a separate Vue app, can join an
existing provider: pass `useDnDContext()` to `provideDnDContext(app, context)` before
mounting it. Hit-testing and the overlay work across shadow roots.

## Other windows of the app

An app may show part of itself in another window: a popup it opens with `window.open`, a
detached panel, a Document Picture-in-Picture window. It renders there with a teleport,
under the same provider. Open the wishlist in a window and sort it there: the overlay is in
the popup.

<example height="26rem" hint="Open the wishlist in a window, then sort it there" name="provider-windows">



</example>

Name the window when you open it:

```ts
const dnd = useDnD();

function detach() {
  const popup = window.open('', 'inspector', 'popup,width=420,height=560')!;
  const release = dnd.addWindow(popup);       // listen there, until it closes
  popup.addEventListener('pagehide', release);
  target.value = popup.document.body;         // <Teleport :to="target">…</Teleport>
}
```

- Drags work in that window as on the page: they start there, sort and hit its targets,
auto-scroll it, and show the overlay in its `<body>`. Its frames run them, so a page
hidden behind the popup doesn't slow them down.
- A pointer or keyboard drag stays in the window it started in: the browser sends a window's
input to that window only. Items with [`native`](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/native) cross between the
windows, carried by the browser's own drag and drop.
- A component rendered into the window when it mounts is found on its own. Content a
teleport moves there later (a panel that detaches) is not: that is what `addWindow` is
for.
- The provider injects its styles into the window, and lets go of it when it closes.
- A [sensor of your own](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/sensors#a-sensor-of-your-own) listens in every window
with `context.onWindow((view) => useEventListener(view.document, …))`.

## SSR and Nuxt

The provider is SSR-safe. Lists and items render on the server like any other markup. The
overlay and the live region are teleported and mount on the client only, so they never
cause a hydration mismatch. Default ids come from Vue's `useId()` and match between server
and client.

In Nuxt, the module registers `DnDProvider` globally and auto-imports the composables: see
[installation](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/getting-started/installation#nuxt).

---

- **Page:** The overlay
- **Source:** https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/overlay
- **Description:** What follows the pointer while you drag — the default clone and how to style it, overlay components that change as you drag, several items at once, its size, and where it renders.

While you drag, a box follows the pointer: the **overlay**. The dragged element itself
stays where it was, as the slot it will land in. On drop, the overlay flies to that slot
and disappears.

The overlay is teleported to `body`, outside your components. By default it shows a clone
of the dragged element.

<example height="22rem" hint="Type in a row, tick it, then drag it by its grip: the copy keeps the values and the chart" name="overlay">



</example>

## The default clone

The clone is taken at pickup, before anything moves. It is a deep copy of the element:

- Form values and `<canvas>` pixels are copied.
- The computed styles the element would lose outside its list are inlined: inherited
fonts and colors, styles that match through ancestors (`.list li { … }`), table cell
widths. A table row comes wrapped in a table of its own.
- `id`s and `data-dnd-*` attributes are stripped, and the clone is `aria-hidden`.
- Ripples and other press effects of UI kits (Vuetify, Quasar, PrimeVue, Naive UI) are
left out.

In the table above, a row you typed in travels with its text, its amount, its tick and its
chart, in a table of its own whose cells keep the widths of the real ones.

Mark anything else that shouldn't travel with **data-dnd-no-clone**: a menu button, a
tooltip, a selection mark. The remove button of each row stays behind:

```vue [ExpenseRow.vue]
<tr ref="el" class="row">
  …
  <td><button type="button" aria-label="Remove" data-dnd-no-clone @click="emit('remove')">×</button></td>
</tr>
```

### Backgrounds aren't guessed

The clone shows the element as it is. A row that has no background of its own, because its
list paints it (an `<li>` in a white `<ul>`, a `v-list-item`, a table row), gives a
**see-through** clone. Give it the list's background in CSS, here on the cells:

```vue [ExpenseRow.vue]
<style scoped>
[data-dnd-overlay] .row td {
  background: color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 4%, Canvas);
}
</style>
```

The clone keeps the element's classes and attributes, Vue's scope attribute included, so
the rule works in the row's scoped style as well as in a global stylesheet. The other way
out is a background on the row itself. Icons and tiles meant to float stay transparent on
purpose.

## Styling the box

The box is the element with `data-dnd-overlay`. It is `position: fixed`, on top
(`z-index: 9999`), `pointer-events: none` and `inert`, and its value says what it is doing:

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      <code>
        data-dnd-overlay
      </code>
    </th>
    
    <th>
      When
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        "dragging"
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      It follows the pointer.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        "dropping"
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      It lands on its slot, flies back, or waits for an async <code>
        onBeforeDrop
      </code>
      
      .
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

A lifted look while dragging, gone as it lands:

```css
[data-dnd-overlay='dragging'] .row td {
  box-shadow: 0 14px 20px -16px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.7);
}
```

The box moves with `transform` and takes its size as `width` and `height`: style what is
inside it, not the box. The clone fills it, with `width: 100%`, `height: 100%` and
`transform: none` set on its root: turn or grow it with the `rotate` and `scale` properties, which
transitions and keyframes both animate. Recipes in [animations](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/animations).

## Overlay components

To show something other than the clone, pass a component. It renders inside the box and
gets the drag as props, which change while you drag: where the drag is, whether that place
takes it, whether the drop copies, and the drop itself.

<example height="26.5rem" hint="Drag a ticket over the columns: Done takes approved ones and stamps them; hold Alt to copy" name="overlay-live">



</example>

```vue [TicketOverlay.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue';
import type { DnDStatus, DragItem, DragMode, Over } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const props = defineProps<{ items: DragItem[]; over: Over | null; accepted: boolean; status: DnDStatus; mode: DragMode }>();
const ticket = computed(() => props.items[0]?.item as Ticket);

const state = computed(() => {
  if (props.status === 'dropping') return props.over ? 'landed' : 'back'; // a cancel flies back
  if (!props.over) return 'free';
  return props.accepted ? 'ok' : 'refused';
});
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Fills the overlay box, which takes the size of the slot. -->
  <div class="ticket-overlay" :data-state="state">
    {{ ticket.title }}
    <span v-if="mode === 'copy'" class="copy">+ copy</span>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.ticket-overlay { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
.ticket-overlay[data-state='refused'] { background: color-mix(in srgb, #ef4444 8%, Canvas); }
</style>
```
