## Before and after

### A draggable and a drop zone

**v2**

```vue [Card.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeDraggable } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const props = defineProps<{ card: Card }>();
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');

const { isDragging } = makeDraggable(el, {
  groups: ['task'],
  dragHandle: '.handle',
  data: () => props.card,
});
</script>

<template>
  <div ref="el" tabindex="0" :class="{ dragging: isDragging }">
    <span class="handle">⋮⋮</span>
    {{ card.title }}
  </div>
</template>
```

```vue [Zone.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeDroppable } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const emit = defineEmits<{ drop: [cards: Card[]] }>();
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');

const { isDragOver, isAllowed } = makeDroppable(el, {
  groups: ['task'],
  events: {
    onDrop: (e) => emit('drop', e.draggedItems.map((item) => item.data as Card)),
  },
});
</script>

<template>
  <div ref="el" :class="{ over: isDragOver && isAllowed }"><slot /></div>
</template>
```

**v3**

```vue [Card.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeDraggable } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const props = defineProps<{ card: Card }>();
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');

const { isDragging } = makeDraggable(el, {
  id: () => props.card.id,   // read back as `active.id`
  type: 'task',              // matched by the targets' `accept`
  handle: '.handle',
  data: () => props.card,
});
</script>

<template>
  <div ref="el" :class="{ dragging: isDragging }">
    <button type="button" class="handle" :aria-label="`Move ${card.title}`">⋮⋮</button>
    {{ card.title }}
  </div>
</template>
```

```vue [Zone.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeDroppable } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const emit = defineEmits<{ drop: [cards: Card[]] }>();
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');

const { isOver, isAccepting } = makeDroppable(el, {
  accept: 'task',
  onDrop: (e) => emit('drop', e.active.items.map((item) => item.data as Card)),
});
</script>

<template>
  <div ref="el" :class="{ over: isOver && isAccepting }"><slot /></div>
</template>
```

- The card gets `tabindex`, `role` and the `aria-*` attributes by itself. A `<button>` handle
is focusable, and keyboard drags start from it.
- `groups` became `type` on the draggable and `accept` on the target. The callbacks left the
`events` object.
- `isOver` without `isAccepting` is a target that refuses the drag: a drop there flies back.

### A sortable list

**v2**

```vue [TaskList.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeDroppable, type IDragEvent } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';
import TaskItem from './TaskItem.vue';

const tasks = defineModel<Task[]>({ required: true });
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');

makeDroppable(
  el,
  {
    events: {
      onDrop(e: IDragEvent) {
        const r = e.helpers.suggestSort('vertical');
        if (r) tasks.value = r.targetItems as Task[];
      },
    },
  },
  () => tasks.value,
);
</script>

<template>
  <div ref="el">
    <TransitionGroup name="list">
      <TaskItem v-for="(task, index) in tasks" :key="task.id" :task="task" :index="index" :tasks="tasks" />
    </TransitionGroup>
  </div>
</template>
```

```vue [TaskItem.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeDraggable } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const props = defineProps<{ task: Task; index: number; tasks: Task[] }>();
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');

const { isDragging } = makeDraggable(el, { id: props.task.id }, () => [props.index, props.tasks]);
</script>

<template>
  <div ref="el" :class="{ 'is-dragging': isDragging }">{{ task.title }}</div>
</template>
```

**v3**

```vue [TaskList.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeSortableList } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';
import TaskItem from './TaskItem.vue';

const tasks = defineModel<Task[]>({ required: true });
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');

const { items } = makeSortableList(el, { items: tasks });
</script>

<template>
  <ul ref="el">
    <TaskItem v-for="task in items" :key="task.id" :task="task" />
  </ul>
</template>
```

```vue [TaskItem.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeSortableItem } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const props = defineProps<{ task: Task }>();
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');

const { isPlaceholder } = makeSortableItem(el, { item: () => props.task });
</script>

<template>
  <li ref="el" :class="{ slot: isPlaceholder }">{{ task.title }}</li>
</template>
```

- Render `items`, the draft: it reorders while you drag. `tasks` gets the new order on drop,
and `defineModel` emits `update:modelValue`.
- No index, no payload, no `onDrop`, no `<TransitionGroup>`: the rows slide by themselves.
- The dragged row stays in the list as the slot it will land in. Style it with `isPlaceholder`
or `[data-dnd-placeholder]` instead of hiding it.

### Lists that share items

**v2**

```ts [Board.vue]
// Each column's makeDroppable calls this from its onDrop, with its array as the payload.
function applySort(e: IDragEvent) {
  const r = e.helpers.suggestSort('vertical');
  if (!r) return;

  const src = e.draggedItems[0]?.items;
  const tgt = e.hoveredDraggable?.items ?? e.dropZone?.items;

  if (src === todo.value) todo.value = r.sourceItems as Task[];
  else if (src === done.value) done.value = r.sourceItems as Task[];

  if (!r.sameList) {
    if (tgt === todo.value) todo.value = r.targetItems as Task[];
    else if (tgt === done.value) done.value = r.targetItems as Task[];
  }
}
```

**v3**

```vue [Column.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { toRef, useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeSortableList } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';
import TaskItem from './TaskItem.vue';

const props = defineProps<{ column: { id: string; tasks: Task[] } }>();
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');

const { items } = makeSortableList(el, {
  id: props.column.id,                   // `from.list` and `to.list` in drop events
  items: toRef(props.column, 'tasks'),   // writable: the parent passes a reactive column
  group: 'board',                        // same name: tasks move between these lists
});
</script>

<template>
  <ul ref="el">
    <TaskItem v-for="task in items" :key="task.id" :task="task" />
  </ul>
</template>
```

```vue [Board.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { reactive } from 'vue';
import Column from './Column.vue';

const columns = reactive([
  { id: 'todo', tasks: [{ id: 't1', title: 'Write the docs' }] },
  { id: 'done', tasks: [] },
]);
</script>

<template>
  <Column v-for="column in columns" :key="column.id" :column="column" />
</template>
```

The drop writes both arrays, the one the task left and the one it entered. `TaskItem.vue` is
the one from the sortable list above. A palette that hands out copies was `suggestCopy()`
and a `copyOnly` flag; now it is a list:

```ts [Palette.vue]
makeSortableList(el, {
  items: blocks,
  group: { name: 'board', pull: 'clone', put: false },  // copies go out, nothing comes in
  sort: false,                                          // its own order stays
  clone: (block) => ({ ...block, id: crypto.randomUUID() }),
});
```

For a Pinia store or other state you don't write directly, pass `items` as a getter, call
`e.preventDefault()` in `onDrop` and apply `e.result`: see
[controlled lists](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/shared-lists#controlled-lists).

### A custom overlay

**v2**

```ts [TaskItem.vue]
makeDraggable(el, {
  render: markRaw(TaskOverlay),
  data: () => props.task,
});
```

```vue [TaskOverlay.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue';
import { useDnDProvider } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const { entities } = useDnDProvider();
const task = computed(() => {
  const [node] = entities.draggingMap.keys();
  return node ? (entities.draggableMap.get(node)?.data?.() as Task) : null;
});
</script>

<template>
  <div class="task-preview">{{ task?.title }}</div>
</template>
```

**v3**

```ts [TaskItem.vue]
makeDraggable(el, {
  id: () => props.task.id,
  overlay: TaskOverlay,
  data: () => props.task,
});
```

```vue [TaskOverlay.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue';
import type { DragItem, Over } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const props = defineProps<{ items: DragItem[]; over: Over | null; accepted: boolean }>();
const task = computed(() => props.items[0]!.data as Task);
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Fills the overlay box, which takes the size of the slot. -->
  <div class="task-preview" :class="{ refused: over && !accepted }">
    {{ task.title }}
    <span v-if="items.length > 1" class="count">{{ items.length }}</span>
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.task-preview { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
</style>
```

- The component gets the drag as props: `items` (every dragged item, the grabbed one first),
`over`, `accepted`, `status`, `mode` and `to`. Declare only the ones you read. For a list's
rows, the list item is `items[0].item`.
- Pass it as it is. Switch it with a `shallowRef`, never a deep `ref`.

The provider's slot changes the same way, and your component no longer positions itself:

**v2**

```vue [App.vue]
<DnDProvider>
  <RouterView />
  <template #preview>
    <MyOverlay />  <!-- moved itself with useDnDProvider().preview.position -->
  </template>
</DnDProvider>
```

**v3**

```vue [App.vue]
<DnDProvider>
  <RouterView />
  <template #overlay="{ items, over, accepted }">
    <MyOverlay :items="items" :over="over" :accepted="accepted" />
  </template>
</DnDProvider>
```

A pop-in that wrapped `DragPreview` in a `<Transition>` becomes `overlay-class` with
`@starting-style`: see [lift, tilt, settle](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/animations#the-overlay-lift-tilt-settle).

### A drop you confirm

**v2**

```ts [Zone.vue]
makeDroppable(el, {
  events: {
    onDrop: (e) =>
      new Promise<void | boolean>((resolve) => {
        if (!window.confirm('Drop here?')) return resolve(false); // keep dragging
        place(e.draggedItems);
        resolve();
      }),
  },
});
```

**v3**

```ts [Zone.vue]
makeDroppable(el, {
  onBeforeDrop: () => (window.confirm('Drop here?') ? 'accept' : 'continue'),
  onDrop: (e) => place(e.active.items),
});
```

A list asks the same way, and a promise lets you open a dialog of your own. The overlay
waits where it was let go until the promise settles:

```ts [Column.vue]
makeSortableList(el, {
  items: toRef(props.column, 'tasks'),
  group: 'board',
  // `ask` opens a dialog and resolves 'accept', 'continue' or 'reject'.
  onBeforeDrop: (e) => (e.sameList ? 'accept' : ask(e)),
});
```

A zone that took only the matching part of a mixed selection (`groupMatch: 'some'`):

**v2**

```ts [Zone.vue]
makeDroppable(el, {
  groups: ['frontend'],
  groupMatch: 'some',
  events: {
    onDrop: (e) => place(e.draggedItems), // only the items of the group arrive
  },
});
```

**v3**

```ts [Zone.vue]
import type { DragItem } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const fits = (item: DragItem) => item.type.length === 0 || item.type.includes('frontend');

makeDroppable(el, {
  accept: 'frontend',
  acceptMode: 'some',
  onBeforeDrop: (e) => e.active.items.filter(fits).map((item) => item.id), // the others fly back
  onDrop: (e) => place(e.active.items.filter(fits)), // `active.items` still lists every dragged item
});
```

Lists do this without code: with `acceptMode: 'some'`, the items their `group.put` takes land,
and the others fly back.

## Pitfalls when upgrading

- **Install v3 with its range.** `^3` in `package.json`: an `npm update` keeps `^2` on v2.
- **Render the draft.** A list renders the `items` that `makeSortableList` returns, not your
array. Rendering your array, nothing moves until the drop.
- **Don't sort twice.** Delete the `suggestSort` code from lists: a list writes each drop into
a writable `items` ref after its `onDrop`. To apply it yourself, call `e.preventDefault()`
and use `e.result`.
- **false refuses the drop.** In v2, an `onDrop` that resolved `false` kept the drag going.
In v3, return `'continue'` from `onBeforeDrop`. A promise returned from `onDrop` is ignored.
- **Lists share only within a group.** A list without one trades with no other list.
- **Key rows by id.** `:key="index"` animates the wrong rows. Pass ids from your data too: a
default id is new for every component instance.
- **No <TransitionGroup>, no transition on transform.** The library moves the rows
itself, and moves would animate twice.
- **Undo the touch workaround.** `touch-action: none` on a whole item keeps the page from
scrolling under a finger; v3 starts touch drags with a long press instead. Keep it on a
handle that should drag at once, with `activation: { touch: { distance: 4 } }`.
- **Remove stale attributes.** The library sets `tabindex`, `role` and the `aria-*` it needs
and never overrides yours, so a leftover `role` or `aria-grabbed` stays as you left it.
- **Restyle the overlay.** `.dnd-kit-preview` is gone: style what is inside
`[data-dnd-overlay='dragging']`, never the box's `transform`. Give the root of an overlay
component `width: 100%; height: 100%`, and take `<DragPreview />` out of your layouts.
- **Auto-scroll is on.** Pass `:auto-scroll="false"` where v2 never scrolled.
- **A band needs no key.** `makeSelectionArea` draws from a plain press on its empty space. Add
a `modifier` to keep v2's Ctrl.
- **One provider, areas inside.** Items can't cross providers. A page that used a provider per
region to keep their rules apart needs one provider and a `makeDragArea` per region.
- **Two arguments.** `makeDraggable` and `makeDroppable` take a ref and an options object, no
payload.

---

- **Page:** Axes, bounds and grids
- **Source:** https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/constraints
- **Description:** Lock drags to one axis, keep them inside a box, snap them to a grid or to guides of your own — for one item, a list or a whole part of the page.

A drag can be held to one axis, kept inside a box, snapped to a grid, or bent by a rule of
your own. The rules are **modifiers**: they adjust the drag's offset on every frame. Set
them on one draggable, on a list, or on a part of the page, and the overlay, the drop
targets and the drop all follow them.

## Lock an axis

Clips on a timeline slide along their track. Turn the lock off and they can change tracks
too.

<example height="22rem" hint="Drag a clip; turn the lock off and drag it to the other track" name="axis-timeline">



</example>

```ts [TimelineClip.vue]
const { isDragging } = makeDraggable(el, {
  id: () => props.clip.id,
  axis: () => (props.locked ? 'x' : undefined),
});
```

`axis: 'x'` moves only horizontally, `'y'` only vertically. `makeDraggable`, `makeSortableList`,
`makeSortableTree`, `makeSortableItem` and `makeDragArea` all take it:

```ts
makeSortableList(listRef, { items: tracks, axis: 'y' });
```

- The lock runs **after every modifier**, so it holds whatever they do: a snap or a bound can't
push the item off its line.
- The line is in the content, not on the screen: it moves with the list (or the parent) the drag
started in. Scroll the page mid-drag and the item stays on its row.
- An item's own `axis` wins over its list's or tree's, and a draggable's (or its list's) wins over
its drag area's.
- It is read when a drag starts, so a getter can toggle it, as above.
- A tree locked to `'y'` still nests: the depth then comes from hovering the middle of a row.

<tip>

Prefer `axis` to the `restrictToVerticalAxis` and `restrictToHorizontalAxis` modifiers. They do the
same thing, but as ordinary modifiers they run in the middle of the chain, and a modifier after
them (a grid snapping both axes) can move the item off the axis again.

</tip>

## Modifiers

A modifier adjusts the drag's offset on every frame. Its result moves the overlay **and** is the
point where targets are looked for, so a list sorts by the locked, bounded or snapped position,
and the drop's `position` is where the box ended up.

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Modifier
    </th>
    
    <th>
      What it does
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        restrictToParent
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Keeps the overlay inside the container the drag started in: the sortable list, or a plain draggable's parent element.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        restrictToElement(target)
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Keeps the overlay inside an element: a template ref, a getter or the element itself.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        restrictToWindowEdges
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Keeps the overlay inside the window.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        restrictToFirstScrollableAncestor
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Keeps the overlay inside the first scrollable ancestor of the dragged element.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        snapToGrid(size)
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Snaps the overlay to a grid (below).
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        snapCenterToCursor
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Centers the overlay under the pointer instead of keeping the grab offset.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        restrictToVerticalAxis
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Moves only vertically. Prefer <code>
        axis: 'y'
      </code>
      
      .
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        restrictToHorizontalAxis
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Moves only horizontally. Prefer <code>
        axis: 'x'
      </code>
      
      .
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

`modifiers` is an option of the provider, of drag areas, of lists and trees, and of draggables
and sortable items. Every one but the provider's also takes a ref or a getter, read when the
drag starts.

### Keep it inside

A self view in a video call stays on the screen. Switch the bound and drag it far out:

<example height="29rem" hint="Drag the self view out of the screen with each bound" name="bounds-pip">



</example>

```ts [SelfView.vue]
const { isDragging } = makeDraggable(el, {
  id: 'self-view',
  modifiers: () => props.modifiers, // [restrictToParent], [restrictToWindowEdges] or []
});
```

- `restrictToParent` holds it on the screen, its parent element. For a sortable item, the
"parent" is its list, wherever the list sits in the DOM.
- `restrictToWindowEdges` lets it leave the screen but not the window. Dropped off the
screen, it isn't on a drop target, so it flies back.
- Without a bound it goes anywhere.

A bound keeps the **overlay** inside, at the size it has: with `overlayFit: 'slot'`, a box
that grows over a list of wider items is kept inside at its new size.

### Snap to a grid

The nodes of a flowchart snap to the canvas grid. Switch the cell size and the glide:

<example height="29rem" hint="Drag a node; switch the grid and smooth" name="snap-canvas">



</example>

```ts [FlowNode.vue]
const { isDragging } = makeDraggable(el, {
  id: () => props.node.id,
  modifiers: () => [snapToGrid({ x: props.grid, y: props.grid, smooth: props.smooth })],
});
```

`snapToGrid(24)` snaps both axes to 24 px cells. An object sets more:

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Option
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Meaning
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        x
      </code>
      
      , <code>
        y
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The cell size in pixels, per axis. Leave one out to snap the other only: <code>
        { y: 15 }
      </code>
      
       snaps an event to quarter hours and lets it move freely across the days.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        origin
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        'container'
      </code>
      
       (default): the overlay's top-left corner lands on grid lines drawn from the container's top-left — the sortable list, or a plain draggable's parent. <code>
        'delta'
      </code>
      
      : the offset itself is rounded, so an item that started off the grid stays off it and moves by whole cells from where it was. Pick it for items placed anywhere (a free canvas) that should keep their own alignment.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        smooth
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        true
      </code>
      
       or <code>
        { duration, easing }
      </code>
      
      : the overlay glides between cells (80 ms by default). Targets use the snapped position at once.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

With `origin: 'container'`, draw the grid from the container's border box: the canvas
above has its frame as a `box-shadow`, not a `border`, so its lines start at its very edge.

### Your own modifier

Boxes on a slide jump onto the edges and centers of the others when they come close, and
pink guides show the lines they sit on:

<example height="26rem" hint="Drag a box next to another one, or to the middle of the slide" name="magnet-guides">



</example>

```ts [Slide.vue]
import type { Modifier } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

/** Near a line, the box jumps onto it. */
const magnet: Modifier = ({ transform, overlayRect, containerRect, active }) => {
  if (!containerRect) return transform;
  const id = String(active.id);
  const left = overlayRect.left - containerRect.left;
  const top = overlayRect.top - containerRect.top;
  return {
    x: transform.x + pull(left, overlayRect.width, lines(id, 'x')),
    y: transform.y + pull(top, overlayRect.height, lines(id, 'y')),
  };
};

// In order: the magnet pulls, then the slide's edges hold.
const modifiers = [magnet, restrictToParent];
```

A modifier gets `transform`, the offset from the drag start as the modifiers before it left
it, and returns a new one. It also gets what it may need to compute it:

Modifiers run on every frame: keep them quick and free of side effects. The guides above
are drawn from the drag's `delta` in a monitor's `onDragMove`, which is the offset after
every modifier. Types in [Modifiers](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/api/modifiers).

## The order

Modifiers from several places run one after another, each from the result of the one before:

1. the provider's `modifiers`;
2. the `modifiers` of the drag area the drag started in;
3. the dragged item's own `modifiers` or, when it has none, its list's or tree's;
4. the drag area's `restrictToArea`;
5. the `axis` lock.

Within one array they run in order, so put snaps and magnets before bounds: a bound last
keeps the box inside whatever the others did. The slide above runs `[magnet, restrictToParent]`;
the other way round, the magnet could pull a box held at the slide's edge a few pixels past it.

An item's `modifiers` **replace** its list's; they don't add to them. The area's bounds come after
the snapping of steps 1–3, so a snapped item still stays inside, and the axis lock comes last of
all.

## Bounded lists keep their ends

A layers panel: rows move up and down only, and never leave the panel. Drag the top row to
the very bottom:

<example height="26rem" hint="Drag Heading to the bottom, past the panel's edge" name="bounded-layers">



</example>

```ts [Layers.vue]
const { items } = makeSortableList(list, { items: layers, axis: 'y', modifiers: [restrictToParent] });
```

A bound holds the overlay at the box's edge while the pointer goes on. Once the pointer has left
the overlay along the list's axis, the list sorts by the pointer instead, so the first and the
last place stay in reach however you hold the item. Grids keep sorting by the overlay: held at the
edge, it already covers the edge cell.

## Rules for a part of the page

Two areas, two sets of rules. Stickers in Layout snap to its grid and can't leave it;
stickers in Sketch go anywhere, into Layout too. A drag keeps the rules of the area it
started in, and the area whose rules are in force lights up.

<example height="25rem" hint="Drag a sticker in Layout, then one from Sketch into Layout" name="drag-areas">



</example>

```vue [DragArea.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
const area = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('area');
const { isDragging } = makeDragArea(area, {
  modifiers: () => (props.strict ? [snapToGrid(24)] : []),
  restrictToArea: () => props.strict,
});
</script>

<template>
  <div ref="area" class="area" :class="{ busy: isDragging }">
    <Sticker v-for="sticker in stickers" :key="sticker.id" :sticker="sticker" />
  </div>
</template>
```

`makeDragArea` sets rules for the drags that **start inside** its element — plain draggables and
sortable items alike, which then need no rules of their own. Keep one `DnDProvider` for the
whole app, and give a board, a canvas or a feed an area of its own.

Every option takes a value, a ref or a getter, read when a press or a drag starts. The area
returns `isDragging` (a drag that started here is running, as the lit frame above shows) and
`isAutoScrolling` (auto-scroll is moving its container). Full reference:
[makeDragArea](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/api/make-drag-area).

### How areas combine

- A drag follows the area it **started in**, even after it leaves it. Passing over an area changes
nothing, except its `autoScroll`: that one applies to every drag that scrolls its container.
- Nested areas don't merge: the closest one wins. `disabled` is the exception, and it is
inherited: an area that is off turns off the areas inside it too.
- Collision detection, keyboard keys and announcements stay provider-wide.

<note>

Why not a second `DnDProvider` around the board? Providers are independent: a drag never crosses
from one to another, so the board's items could never leave it. Nest a provider only when a part
of the page needs provider-wide settings of its own and its items stay inside it. See
[The provider](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/provider).

</note>

## Leave it where it's dropped

The timeline, the call, the flowchart, the slide and the areas above all keep each item where it
was dropped. Every drag event carries `position`: the dragged box's top-left corner inside the
target, from its padding edge and with its scroll — the `left` and `top` that put an absolutely
positioned item right there. It comes after the modifiers, so a snapped node lands on the grid.

```ts [Flowchart.vue]
makeDroppable(canvas, { id: 'canvas' });
useDnDMonitor({
  onDragEnd({ active, over, position }) {
    const node = nodes.value.find((item) => item.id === active.id);
    if (!node || over?.id !== 'canvas' || !position) return;
    node.x = Math.round(position.x);
    node.y = Math.round(position.y);
  },
});
```

More on free dragging and drop targets in [Drag and drop](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/drag-and-drop).

---

- **Page:** Trees
- **Source:** https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/trees
- **Description:** Outlines, menus, org charts and backlogs with makeSortableTree — rendered flat with depths, nested by dragging sideways or hovering a row, with rules, collapsed nodes, an insertion line and lists in the same group.

A tree is a sortable list whose rows have depths. Drag a section left or right to change
its level, or hold it over the middle of another section to drop it inside. The numbers
follow the drag.

<example height="45.5rem" hint="Drag a section sideways, or switch the nesting mode" name="tree-outline">



</example>

## Rendered flat

`makeSortableTree` takes your nested data and returns the visible nodes as a **flat list**,
in order, each with its `depth`. You render that list and indent the rows yourself. Every
row stays a sibling in one container, so rows slide and animate like the rows of a list.

```vue [Outline.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeSortableTree } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';
import Heading from './Heading.vue';

interface Section { id: string; title: string; children?: Section[] }

const outline = ref<Section[]>([
  { id: 'start', title: 'Getting started', children: [{ id: 'install', title: 'Installation' }] },
  { id: 'faq', title: 'FAQ' },
]);

const root = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('root');
const { items, projected } = makeSortableTree(root, {
  items: outline,     // the root nodes: a writable ref takes every drop
  indentation: 24,    // px per level: match the rows' indentation
  maxDepth: 2,
});
</script>

<template>
  <ol ref="root">
    <Heading v-for="node in items" :key="node.key" :node="node" />
  </ol>
</template>
```

```vue [Heading.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeSortableItem, type FlatNode } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const props = defineProps<{ node: FlatNode<{ id: string; title: string }> }>();
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');
makeSortableItem(el, { id: () => props.node.key });
</script>

<template>
  <li ref="el" :style="{ marginInlineStart: `${node.depth * 24}px` }">{{ node.item.title }}</li>
</template>
```

Rows use `makeSortableItem`, like the rows of a list. Indent them with a margin, not a
padding: the row itself then moves with its depth. The overlay takes the slot's width and
lands on its level, and a change of depth slides like any other move. A padding would
indent only what is inside the row, and the overlay, a copy of the row at pickup, would
keep the level the drag started at. `items` holds `FlatNode`s:

    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

      <code>
        key
      </code>
    </td>

      The node's key (<code>
        getKey
      </code>
      
      , default <code>
        node.id
      </code>

       and the row's <code>

      <code>

Since `items` is the draft, anything you compute from it follows the drag: the demo
numbers its sections from `items`, so "2.1" becomes "3.1" while you move. `projected` is
where the dragged node would land, `{ depth, parentKey }`, or `null` while it isn't over
this tree.

Children are read from `node.children` and written there. Data with another shape takes
`getChildren` and `setChildren`; the [org chart](#rules) below keeps them in `members`:

```ts
makeSortableTree(root, {
  items: org,
  getChildren: (member) => member.members,
  setChildren: (member, members) => { member.members = members; },
});
```

## Nesting

A drag changes the depth in two ways, both on by default:

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      <code>
        nesting
      </code>
    </th>
    
    <th>
      The depth comes from…
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        'offset'
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Dragging sideways: every <code>
        indentation
      </code>
      
       pixels left or right is a level up or down, as far as the rows around the slot allow.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        'hover'
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Holding the drag over the middle of a row: the drop goes inside it, as its first child.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        'both'
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Either. The default.
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

Set `indentation` to what your rows add per level (`24` by default), so the slot follows
the pointer: in the demo, switch to `40` and drag sideways. With `'hover'` alone, a
sideways drag keeps the level, and only a row's middle nests. Both options take a ref or
a getter and apply to the next drag.

With `axis: 'y'` (or `restrictToVerticalAxis`), the drag can't move sideways, but rows
still nest by hovering.

## Rules

Engineering takes people and teams; Leadership is locked; nothing goes deeper than a team
in a team. Open and close the teams: the rows they show and hide slide in and out.

<example height="41rem" hint="Move people between teams; try Leadership and a third level" name="tree-org">



</example>

```ts [OrgTree.vue]
const { items } = makeSortableTree(root, {
  items: org,
  getChildren: (member) => member.members,
  setChildren: (member, members) => { member.members = members; },
  // Only teams take members, and a locked team takes no one.
  canNest: (_member, team) => team.kind === 'team' && !team.locked,
  maxDepth: 2,
  collapsed,
  animateChanges: true,
});
```

```ts [OrgRow.vue]
// A locked row doesn't drag (and says so with `aria-disabled`).
makeSortableItem(el, { id: () => props.node.key, disabled: () => !!props.node.item.locked });
```

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Option
    </th>
    
    <th>
      Limits
    </th>
  </tr>
</thead>

<tbody>
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        canNest(node, parent)
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Whether <code>
        node
      </code>
      
       may go under <code>
        parent
      </code>
      
      . A multi-drag asks for every dragged node. Roots are always allowed.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        maxDepth
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      The deepest depth allowed, roots being <code>
        0
      </code>
      
      . The dragged node's descendants count: a team with members goes no deeper than <code>
        maxDepth - 1
      </code>
      
      .
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        disabled
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      On a row: it doesn't drag. On the tree: nothing drags from it or drops into it.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        group.put
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Whether the tree takes items from other lists and trees at all.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        onBeforeDrop
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Anything else, decided on drop: see <a href="/docs/guides/drop-decisions">
        deciding a drop
      </a>
      
      .
    </td>
  </tr>
</tbody>
</table>

When a rule refuses a depth, the slot takes the deepest depth that passes: drag Noor below
Raj and to the right, and the slot stays at the top level, since Leadership is locked and
Raj is a person. Where no depth passes, the slot doesn't move there. Copies and nodes from
`createItem` follow `canNest` and `maxDepth` too.

### Collapsed nodes

`collapsed` is a `Set` of keys whose children are hidden, as a ref or a getter. Their
children aren't in `items`; `node.collapsed` and `node.hasChildren` drive the button:

```ts
const collapsed = ref(new Set<Key>());
const toggle = (key: Key) => (collapsed.value.has(key) ? collapsed.value.delete(key) : collapsed.value.add(key));
```

A dragged node takes its whole subtree along, collapsed or not. With `animateChanges: true`, the
rows a node shows or hides as it opens or closes animate in and out, and so do changes to
the data that no drag made.

## An insertion line

Drag a template from the left into the menu, or move an item: the menu stays still and a
line shows where the drop goes, starting at the level it lands at. Over the middle of a
page or group, the row lights up instead.

<example height="31rem" hint="Drag a template into the menu, or move an item sideways" name="tree-menu">



</example>

With `placeholder: 'indicator'`, the tree doesn't move while you drag. Each row reads its
`indicator` and draws the line:

```vue [MenuRow.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed, useTemplateRef } from 'vue';
import { makeSortableItem, type FlatNode } from '@vue-dnd-kit/core';

const props = defineProps<{ node: FlatNode<MenuItem>; indent: number }>();
const el = useTemplateRef<HTMLElement>('el');
const { indicator } = makeSortableItem(el, { id: () => props.node.key });

// 'inside': the drop goes into this row. Otherwise a line before or after it.
const inside = computed(() => indicator.value?.side === 'inside');
const line = computed(() => {
  const value = indicator.value;
  if (!value || value.side === 'inside') return null;
  // From the level the drop lands at, measured from this row's own level.
  return { side: value.side, left: `${((value.depth ?? 0) - props.node.depth) * props.indent}px` };
});
</script>

<template>
  <div ref="el" class="item" :class="{ inside }" :style="{ marginLeft: `${node.depth * indent}px` }">
    {{ node.item.title }}
    <span v-if="line" class="line" :class="line.side" :style="{ left: line.left }" />
  </div>
</template>

<style scoped>
.item { position: relative; }
.item.inside { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1.5px #42b883; }
.line { position: absolute; right: 0; height: 2px; background: #42b883; }
.line.before { top: -3px; }
.line.after { bottom: -3px; }
</style>
```

`indicator` adds `depth` and `parentKey` in trees: the level and the parent the dropped
nodes get. Dragging sideways moves the line between levels, and the keyboard moves the line
too. In this mode, a drop outside the tree cancels.

The templates are plain draggables (`makeDraggable`) with `data`. The tree turns them into
new nodes with `createItem`, at the line's position and depth:

```ts [MenuTree.vue]
let created = 0;
makeSortableTree(root, {
  items: menu,
  placeholder: 'indicator',
  maxDepth: 1,
  canNest: (_item, parent) => parent.kind !== 'link',
  createItem: (active) => {
    const template = active.data as { title: string; kind: MenuItem['kind'] };
    return { id: `new-${++created}`, title: `New ${template.title.toLowerCase()}`, kind: template.kind };
  },
});
```

The bar above the menu renders `menu`, the saved data, not `items`: it changes on drop
only.

## Trees and lists in one group

A story moved into the backlog keeps its tasks, out of sight, and brings them back to the
roadmap. Hold <kbd value="Alt">



</kbd>

 while dragging out of the roadmap to copy instead.

<example height="29.5rem" hint="Move Saved cards to the backlog and back; Alt copies" name="tree-backlog">



</example>

A tree and a list with the same `group` exchange nodes, as two lists do. A node keeps its
subtree wherever it goes: the list just doesn't show it. The same row component serves
both, since `makeSortableItem({ item })` is keyed by whichever list or tree owns the row.

Copies work as in lists (`clone`, `pull: 'clone'`, the copy key), but `clone` must return
the copy **with its whole subtree**, and every node in it needs a new key:

```ts [Roadmap.vue]
let copies = 0;
const copy = (work: Work): Work => ({ ...work, id: `${work.id}-copy-${++copies}`, children: work.children?.map(copy) });

makeSortableTree(root, {
  items: roadmap,
  group: 'work',
  canNest: (work, parent) => RANK[parent.kind] < RANK[work.kind],
  maxDepth: 2,
  clone: copy,
});
```

See [lists that share items](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/shared-lists) for groups, copying and
`createItem`.

## The drop

The tree's drop event is a list's, with `parentKey` added to `from` and `to`:

```ts
makeSortableTree(root, {
  items: outline,
  onDrop: (e) => {
    console.log(e.keys, e.from.parentKey, '→', e.to.parentKey, e.to.index);
  },
});
```

`to.index` is the position among the new siblings, counted after the node left its old
place. On drop, the library gives the changed nodes their new children (`setChildren`) and
writes a new root array into your ref.

`e.result.get(treeId)` is the new tree as a new root array: the nodes on the changed paths
are copies, untouched subtrees are shared, and your nodes stay as they are. For a store or
immutable data, pass a getter, call `e.preventDefault()` and save `e.result` (see
[deciding a drop](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/drop-decisions#stores-and-servers-controlled-lists)). Copies
are made with `withChildren(node, children)`, by default `{ ...node }` with the new
children; pass your own for class instances.

## onBeforeDrop

```ts
makeSortableList(listRef, {
  items: tasks,
  onBeforeDrop: (e) => (e.items.some((task) => task.locked) ? 'reject' : 'accept'),
});
```

Lists, trees, drop targets (`makeDroppable`) and monitors (`useDnDMonitor`) take an
`onBeforeDrop`. It runs when the drag is let go, before anything changes, and its answer
decides:

<table>

    </td>

        'reject'
      </code>
      
       or <code>
        false
      </code>

Lists and trees pass a `SortableDropEvent`: `keys`, `items`, `from`, `to`, `mode`, `sameList` and
`result`, the new arrays of every list the drop changes. Drop targets and monitors get the generic
`DnDEvent`: `active`, `over`, `position` and `source`. See [events](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/api/events).

## A rule while dragging, or on release

Email and Chat both take attachments of 10 MB at most. Drag **demo.mov** over each: Email
refuses it while you hover, Chat takes it and sends it back when you let go.

<example height="27rem" hint="Drag a file over 10 MB into each place" name="drop-rules">



</example>

```ts [Column.vue]
// Asked while dragging: a refused drag never enters the list.
group: { name: 'attachments', put: ({ items }) => fits(items as Attachment[]) },

// Asked on release: the drag enters the list, then flies back.
onBeforeDrop: (e) => (fits(e.items) ? 'accept' : 'reject'),
```

Use `group.put` for what is known from the items alone (a type, a flag, a count): the
user learns it before letting go. Use `onBeforeDrop` for what depends on the place, the
user's answer or the server's. The target's own rules come first: over a list or a target
that refuses the drag, the drop is cancelled and its `onBeforeDrop` isn't asked.

### Accepting some of the items

Some rules can only be checked on release, against a server. Seats of this workshop are booked
by others too: on release, the list asks the server how many are left, and takes that many of
the people dragged in. Tick a few, and drag them in together.

<example height="28.5rem" hint="Tick three people, drag one of them into the workshop" name="drop-partial">



</example>

```ts [Column.vue]
makeSortableList(list, {
  items: toRef(props.column, 'people'),
  group: 'workshop',
  // Some keys: those land, the others fly back to where they came from.
  onBeforeDrop: async (e) => {
    const { free } = await seatsLeft(props.column.people.length); // the overlay waits
    return e.keys.slice(0, free);
  },
  onDrop: (e) => {
    selection.delete(...e.accepted); // the ones sent back stay selected
    notice.value = `${e.accepted.length} booked, ${e.rejected.length} back to the waiting list`;
  },
});
```

In a [multi-drag](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/multi-drag), the keys you return land together and the rest
fly back to their places. `onDrop` then sees them in `e.accepted` and `e.rejected`, and its
`e.result` is the final one. An empty array accepts nothing: the drop is refused.

## Keep dragging: 'continue'

`'continue'` cancels the drop, not the drag. Answer **Keep dragging** in the dialog above:
the item stays in hand from where it was, the page goes back into drag mode, and the user
carries on.

- With a mouse or a pen, the item follows the pointer with no button held. The next release — a
click — drops it, and that click never reaches the page underneath.
- A touch takes the item again where the finger lands; lifting the finger drops it.
- A keyboard drag goes on: the arrows move the item, <kbd value="Space">



</kbd>

 or <kbd value="Enter">



</kbd>


drop it.
- <kbd value="Escape">



</kbd>

 cancels it, as any drag.
- The next drop asks `onBeforeDrop` again.

Monitors hear `onDragResume`, and screen readers hear that the item wasn't dropped and is still
moving (override the text with the provider's `announcements.onDragResume`).

```ts
useDnDMonitor({
  onDragResume() {
    hint.value = 'Still dragging: click to drop, Esc to cancel';
  },
});
```

## Asking the user

`onBeforeDrop` may return a promise. Open a dialog, and resolve the promise with the button the
user picks:

```ts [Column.vue]
const { items } = makeSortableList(list, {
  id: props.column.id,
  items: toRef(props.column, 'tasks'),
  group: 'release',
  onBeforeDrop: (e) => (props.column.confirm && !e.sameList ? props.ask(e) : 'accept'),
});
```

```ts [Board.vue]
type Answer = 'accept' | 'continue' | 'reject';
const question = shallowRef<{ title: string; resolve: (answer: Answer) => void } | null>(null);

/** Opens the dialog: `onBeforeDrop` waits for the button the user picks. */
const ask = (e: SortableDropEvent<Task>) =>
  new Promise<Answer>((resolve) => {
    question.value = { title: e.items[0]!.title, resolve };
  });
```

While the promise is pending:

- the overlay waits where it was let go, marked `data-dnd-overlay="dropping"`;
- `useDnD()` keeps the state it had at release, and `status` is `'dropping'`;
- the page is out of drag mode: the cursor and text selection are back, so a dialog works as
usual;
- no other drag can start.

<tip>

A modal `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` sits in the top layer, above the waiting overlay. Turn
its `cancel` event (<kbd value="Escape">



</kbd>

) into `'reject'`, as the example does.

</tip>

## The order of the hooks

Reorder the notes, drop one in the trash, then switch an answer and do it again. The panel
lists the hooks of the last drop in the order they ran.

<example height="27.5rem" hint="Move a note or trash one, then switch an answer to reject or continue" name="drop-hooks">



</example>

1. `onBeforeDrop` of every `useDnDMonitor`, in turn. A `'reject'` or a `'continue'` ends the
asking; keys narrow the drop.
2. `onBeforeDrop` of the target: the list or tree the items go into, or the drop target.
3. `onDrop` of the target only: a list that items leave for another one isn't asked, and its new
array is in the target's `e.result`. When items are removed (a trash zone,
`dropOutside: 'remove'`), their list's `onDrop` runs, with `to.index` of `-1`.
4. The default write: each list the drop changes takes its new array.
5. `onDragEnd` of the provider (`@drag-end`) and the monitors. Then the overlay lands, and
`onDragSettle` (`@drag-settle`) says it has.

A refused drop skips to `onDragCancel` (`@drag-cancel`) instead, and the items fly back. A
`'continue'` ends the asking too, with `onDragResume`: the drag goes on, and its next drop
asks again.

Monitors decide before the target, so a veto never comes after a list has already applied a
drop of its own. That makes a monitor the place for rules about every drop of the app:

```ts [Monitor.vue]
const { syncing } = useSync();

// Read-only while syncing: every drop under the provider flies back.
useDnDMonitor({
  onBeforeDrop: () => (syncing.value ? 'reject' : 'accept'),
});
```

## onDrop: told before the write

```ts
makeSortableList(listRef, {
  items: tasks,
  onDrop: (e) => {
    // `tasks` still holds the old order, `e.result` the new one.
    console.log(e.keys, e.from, e.to, e.result.get(e.to.list));
  },
});
```

A list's `onDrop` runs once the drop is accepted, synchronously, right before the list writes it.
To act after the write, use the provider's `@drag-end` or `useDnDMonitor({ onDragEnd })`. On a
plain drop target, `onDrop` is where you change your data: the library moves nothing for it.

## Stores and servers: controlled lists

```ts
const store = useBoardStore();
const { items } = makeSortableList(listRef, {
  id: 'todo',
  group: 'board',
  items: () => store.lists.todo, // a getter: read-only
  onDrop: (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    for (const [listId, next] of e.result) store.setList(listId, next);
  },
});
```

The library writes a drop only into a writable ref. A getter, a `computed` or a `readonly` ref is
never written: call `e.preventDefault()` and apply `e.result` yourself — the new arrays of every
list the drop changes, by list id. `preventDefault()` skips the write into all of them, since
writing only some would lose or duplicate items. Development builds warn when a read-only list's
drop is left to the library.

### Saving to a server first

Move a card with the server **flaky** (every other request fails) or **down**. The card waits
with a badge while the request runs, then lands, or flies back if it failed.

<example height="31.5rem" hint="Move cards, then switch the server to flaky or down" name="drop-server">



</example>

```ts [Column.vue]
const { items } = makeSortableList(list, {
  id: props.id,
  // A getter: the library never writes it. The drop is applied below, once saved.
  items: () => board[props.id]!,
  group: 'sprint',
  onBeforeDrop: async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    try {
      await saveMove(e.keys, e.to);
    } catch {
      return 'reject'; // nothing applied: the card flies back
    }
    for (const [id, tasks] of e.result) board[id] = tasks; // lands in its new place
    return 'accept';
  },
});
```

Apply `e.result` before the promise resolves, and the overlay lands in the new order. When
the request fails, apply nothing and reject: the items fly back, and monitors hear
`onDragCancel`.

The badge comes from the provider's `#overlay` slot, which renders every drag's overlay. A
`DragPreview` shows the usual copy of the card, and the badge sits on top while the request
runs:

```vue [index.vue]
<DnDProvider>
  <Board />
  <template #overlay="{ active }">
    <div class="carried">
      <DragPreview :id="active.id" />
      <span v-if="saving" class="saving">Saving…</span>
    </div>
  </template>
</DnDProvider>
```

## Dropping outside every target

Drag an app off the dock and let go, in each mode.

<example height="24.5rem" hint="Drag an app off the dock and let go" name="drop-outside">

const { items } = makeSortableList(dock, {
  items: apps,
  strategy: 'horizontal',
  dropOutside: () => props.dropOutside,
  // Called on the list the items leave, with `to.index` -1, when they are removed.
  onDrop: (e) => {
    if (e.to.index === -1) notice.value = `Removed ${e.items.map((app) => app.name).join(', ')}`;
  },
});
```

---

- **Page:** Styling
- **Source:** https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/styling
- **Description:** Every state of a drag, styled — data attributes for plain CSS, refs for classes, targets that say yes or no, the overlay and the page while you drag, the default styles, Tailwind and UI kits.

The library styles almost nothing. Each state of a drag reaches you two ways: as a
`data-dnd-*` attribute, for plain CSS, and as a ref the composable returns, for classes
and conditional markup. Use whichever suits your stack, or both.

       mode.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        data-dnd-dragging="pointer"
      </code>
      
       or <code>
        "keyboard"
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      <code>
        <html>
      </code>
    </td>

      For the whole drag.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>

      <code>
        data-dnd-overlay="dragging"
      </code>
      
       or <code>
        "dropping"

```css [TaskRow.vue]
/* The slot a dragged row will land in: a striped gap. */
.row[data-dnd-placeholder] {
  opacity: 1;
  background: repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, color-mix(in srgb, #42b883 16%, transparent) 0 6px, transparent 6px 12px);
}

.row[data-dnd-placeholder] > * {
  visibility: hidden;   /* an empty slot of the row's exact size */
}

/* Selected rows left in place by a multi-drag (`multiple: 'gaps'`). */
.row[data-dnd-dragging] {
  opacity: 0.4;
}

/* The copy in the overlay, while it travels. */
[data-dnd-overlay='dragging'] .row {
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 1.5px #42b883, 0 14px 24px -10px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.55);
}
```

```vue [TaskRow.vue]
<li ref="el" class="row" :aria-selected="selected">
  <span class="title">{{ task.title }}</span>
  <button type="button" data-dnd-no-clone @click.stop="task.done = !task.done">✓</button>
</li>
```

- The overlay's copy of a row keeps its classes and attributes, Vue's scope attribute
included, so `[data-dnd-overlay] .row` works in the row's own `<style scoped>`. The
copy has no `data-dnd-*` marks of its own: a copy of the slot is not a slot.
- Selection has no attribute. Mirror the `selected` ref into one (`aria-selected` above),
or use a class.
- Plain draggables and drop targets (`makeDraggable`, `makeDroppable`) get no `data-dnd-*`
state attributes: style them with their refs.

## The returned refs

The same states as refs, plus the ones the lists and targets have. Each row and list
below prints the refs that are true right now, and its classes come from them. The
Icebox refuses urgent tasks: drag one over it.

<example height="24rem" hint="Drag a task to the other list; Ctrl/⌘-click selects several" name="dnd-refs">



</example>

```vue [RefRow.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
const { isDragging, isPlaceholder, selected } = makeSortableItem(el, { item: () => props.task });
</script>

<template>
  <li ref="el" class="row" :class="{ placeholder: isPlaceholder, dragging: isDragging, selected }">…</li>
</template>

<style scoped>
.row.selected { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1.5px #3b82f6; }
.row.placeholder { opacity: 1; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px #42b883; }   /* beats the default 40% */
.row.placeholder .title { visibility: hidden; }
</style>
```

```vue [RefList.vue]
<script setup lang="ts">
const { items, isOver, isAccepting } = makeSortableList(el, { items, group });
</script>

<template>
  <section :class="{ accepting: isAccepting, over: isOver && isAccepting, refused: isOver && !isAccepting }">…</section>
</template>
```

- `isPlaceholder`: this element is the slot a dragged item will land in. In a multi-drag
in `'group'` mode, the slots of the items travelling along are placeholders too.
- `isDragging`: the item is part of the drag: every dragged item in a multi-drag.
- `isAccepting`: something is being dragged, and this target takes it. Light up the places
where a drop is possible.
- `isOver`: the drag is over this target, whether it takes it or not. `isOver && !isAccepting`
is a refusal: show it.
- `indicator`: where the drop line goes in [indicator mode](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/sortable-lists#an-insertion-line).
- `activation.progress`: from 0 to 1 while a touch long press or a `delay` runs. Fill a
ring with it.

## Drop targets: yes and no

A target has four looks while a drag runs: it takes the drag, it takes it and the pointer
is on it, it refuses it, it refuses it and the pointer is on it. Show all four, and say
it on the dragged item too.

<example height="23rem" hint="Drag a colour over the palettes: the right one invites it, the others don't" name="drop-highlights">



</example>

```ts [Palette.vue]
const { isOver, isAccepting } = makeDroppable(el, { accept: props.tone, onDrop });

const { active } = useDnD();
const state = computed(() => {
  if (!active.value) return '';
  if (isOver.value) return isAccepting.value ? 'over' : 'refused';
  return isAccepting.value ? 'accepting' : 'refusing';
});
```

```css [Palette.vue]
.palette.accepting { border-style: dashed; border-color: #42b883; }          /* an invitation */
.palette.over { border-color: #42b883; background: color-mix(in srgb, #42b883 14%, Canvas); }
.palette.refusing { opacity: 0.45; }                                          /* out of the way */
.palette.refused { border-color: #f43f5e; animation: shake 0.3s; }            /* a drop here is cancelled */
```

The dragged swatch is the provider's `#overlay` slot. It gets `over` and `accepted`:
`accepted` is `false` over a target that refuses the drag.

```vue [index.vue]
<template #overlay="{ active, over, accepted }">
  <div
    class="lifted"
    :class="{ yes: over && accepted, no: over && !accepted }"
    :style="{ background: (active.data as { color: string }).color }"
  >
    <span v-if="over" class="badge">{{ accepted ? '+' : '✕' }}</span>
  </div>
</template>
```

Outside the overlay, `useDnD().over.value?.accepted` says the same. More on overlay
components in [the overlay](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/overlay).

## The overlay and the page

Two attributes cover the rest of a drag: `data-dnd-overlay` on the overlay box, and
`data-dnd-dragging` on `<html>`, `"pointer"` or `"keyboard"`. The bar above the notes
reads the second one, and says which keys work. Turn on the slow save: the overlay stays
`dropping` where you let go, until `onBeforeDrop` resolves, and shows it.

<example height="27rem" hint="Drag a note with the mouse, then with the keyboard; turn on the slow save" name="overlay-theme">



</example>

```css [index.vue]
.bar .pointer,
.bar .keyboard,
html[data-dnd-dragging] .bar .idle { display: none; }

html[data-dnd-dragging='pointer'] .bar .pointer,
html[data-dnd-dragging='keyboard'] .bar .keyboard { display: inline; }
```

```css [StickyNote.vue]
[data-dnd-overlay='dragging'] .note {
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #42b883, 0 22px 30px -14px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6);
}

/* Landing, and waiting for the save. */
[data-dnd-overlay='dropping'] .note { opacity: 0.85; }
[data-dnd-overlay='dropping'] .saving { display: flex; }
```

- `dropping` covers the landing and the wait of an async `onBeforeDrop`. While it waits,
`<html>` is out of drag mode: the page's cursor and text selection are back, so a
confirmation dialog works as usual.
- Style what is **inside** the box. The library moves the box itself with `transform`
and sizes it with `width` and `height`. Its content element, `[data-dnd-overlay-content]`,
fills it and is yours: lift and tilt the whole overlay there (see
[animations](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/animations#the-overlay-lift-tilt-settle)).
- The copy's root has `transform: none` inline: turn or grow it with `rotate` and `scale`.
Transitions and keyframes both run on it: see
[animations](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/animations#the-overlay-lift-tilt-settle).
- The copy shows the element as it is and guesses no background. A row the list paints
(an `<li>` in a white `<ul>`, a table row) needs one: `[data-dnd-overlay] .row { background: Canvas; }`.
- The copy sits in a `<div>` that carries the custom properties the element inherited
(theme colors, `--tw-*`), so they still apply in the overlay, and the copy's own rules
(`in-data-[dnd-overlay]:ring-2`) still beat them. Select the copy by its class, not by
its depth in the box.

## Default styles

The provider injects a few rules once per document. They are wrapped in `:where()`, so
their specificity is zero and any rule of yours wins:

```css
:where([data-dnd-placeholder]) { opacity: 0.4; }
:where([data-dnd-dragging]:not(html)) { opacity: 0.4; }
:where(html[data-dnd-dragging]), :where(html[data-dnd-dragging] *) {
  user-select: none !important;
  overflow-anchor: none !important;
}
:where(html[data-dnd-dragging='pointer']), :where(html[data-dnd-dragging='pointer'] *) {
  cursor: var(--dnd-cursor, grabbing) !important;
  -webkit-touch-callout: none !important;
}
```

`:default-styles="false"` on the provider leaves them out. The library still marks
`<html>`, and still clears the text selection when a drag starts and blocks new selections
until it ends: only the CSS is gone. The rules are injected once, by the first provider that
wants them, and stay: turn them off on every provider of the page.

```vue
<DnDProvider :default-styles="false">
```

## Tailwind CSS

The attributes work as variants: `data-[…]` for the element itself, an arbitrary
variant for an ancestor.

```vue [TaskRow.vue]
<li
  ref="el"
  class="rounded-lg bg-white shadow-sm
         data-[dnd-placeholder]:bg-transparent data-[dnd-placeholder]:opacity-100
         data-[dnd-placeholder]:outline-dashed
         [[data-dnd-overlay=dragging]_&]:shadow-xl"
  :class="{ 'ring-2 ring-emerald-500': selected }"
>
```

```vue [Hint.vue]
<p class="hidden [html[data-dnd-dragging=keyboard]_&]:block">Arrows move · Space drops</p>
```

<note>

The library's looks (the 40% opacities) sit in a cascade layer of their own,
`vue-dnd-kit`, declared before any other. Tailwind v4's utilities and the UI kits built on
it live in layers too, and theirs come later, so they win without `!`. Unlayered CSS wins
anyway.

</note>

In Tailwind v4, `in-data-[dnd-overlay=dragging]:shadow-xl` is a shorter way to write the
ancestor variant.

<warning>

In Vue's scoped CSS, `:global()` takes the whole selector: `:global(html[data-dnd-dragging]) .hint`
compiles to `html[data-dnd-dragging]` alone, and hides the page. Write the ancestor
without it, `html[data-dnd-dragging] .hint`: Vue scopes only the last part.

</warning>

## UI kits

- The composables take a component as well as an element: `useTemplateRef` on a kit's
card or list item works, and the library reads its root element.
- Pass state to the kit's own props where it has them (`:active="selected"`,
`:color="isOver ? 'primary' : undefined"`), and the rest as classes.
- A kit's list items often have no background of their own: the list paints it. Their
copy in the overlay is then see-through. Give it one:```css
[data-dnd-overlay] .v-list-item { background: rgb(var(--v-theme-surface)); }
```
- The copy leaves out the press ripples of Vuetify, Quasar, PrimeVue and Naive UI. Mark
anything else that shouldn't travel, a tooltip or a menu button, with
`data-dnd-no-clone`.

## Don't

- Don't put a CSS `transition` on `transform` or `translate` of sortable items: the
library animates them itself, and cancels such transitions while it measures.
- Don't wrap sortable items in `<TransitionGroup>`: moves would animate twice. Use the
list's `animateChanges`.
- Don't animate `height`, `margin` or `padding` of rows in a [virtual list](/docs/guides/virtual-lists).
- Do stop the transitions you add around drags under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
The library already stops its own.

---

- **Page:** DevTools
- **Source:** https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/devtools
- **Description:** A Vue DnD Kit tab in the Vue DevTools and the Nuxt DevTools — a live mini-map, a joystick that drags for real, live option editing and a log of every drag.

`@vue-dnd-kit/devtools` adds a **Vue DnD Kit** tab to the Vue DevTools (`vite-plugin-vue-devtools`)
and to the Nuxt DevTools. It shows every list, tree and drop target of the page in a live
mini-map, drags any item with a joystick, edits options while the app runs, and logs what each drag
did. It works in development only: nothing of it reaches a production build.

The tab is a page of its own, served by your dev server next to your app, so it can't run inside
these docs. Three steps set it up.

## Install

### 1. Add the packages

```bash
npm i -D @vue-dnd-kit/devtools @vue-dnd-kit/actions
```

`@vue-dnd-kit/actions` is a peer dependency: the tab's moves go through it. npm 7+ and pnpm install
it by themselves; with Yarn 1, add it.

### 2. Add the plugin

<code-group>

```ts [vite.config.ts]
import { defineConfig } from 'vite';
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue';
import vueDevTools from 'vite-plugin-vue-devtools';
import { vueDnDKitDevtools } from '@vue-dnd-kit/devtools/vite';

export default defineConfig({
  // Next to the Vue DevTools plugin: the tab joins its sidebar.
  plugins: [vueDevTools(), vueDnDKitDevtools(), vue()],
});
```

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  // With @vue-dnd-kit/devtools installed, the tab appears in development.
  modules: ['@vue-dnd-kit/nuxt'],
});
```

</code-group>

With Vite, the plugin does three things on the dev server (`vite serve`): it serves the tab at
`/__vue-dnd-kit-devtools/` (under your `base`), adds it to the Vue DevTools, and makes the page
report to it before your app starts. No `app.use()` is needed, and builds are untouched.

With Nuxt, the `@vue-dnd-kit/nuxt` module finds the package, serves the tab, adds it to the Nuxt
DevTools and installs the page's side with a client plugin. `vueDndKit: { devtools: false }` turns
it off.

### 3. Run the app in development

Start the dev server as usual (`vite`, `nuxt dev`) and open the app: the tab is ready. Every
provider of the page shows in it, whichever app it renders in.

### Without the plugins

For a dev server of your own, or a page Vite doesn't serve from an `index.html` (SSR setups),
install the page's side yourself:

```ts [main.ts]
import { createApp } from 'vue';
import { DnDDevtools } from '@vue-dnd-kit/devtools';
import App from './App.vue';

const app = createApp(App);
app.use(DnDDevtools); // before mount: providers set up earlier aren't seen
app.mount('#app');
```

Or import `@vue-dnd-kit/devtools/auto` first in the entry file. Use
`vueDnDKitDevtools({ inject: false })` when the plugin should serve the tab but you install the
page's side yourself; `serveTab()` from `@vue-dnd-kit/devtools/vite` is the middleware that serves
the tab.

<note>

In a production build, `app.use(DnDDevtools)` and the `auto` import shrink to almost nothing:
every entry point checks `process.env.NODE_ENV` first, and bundlers drop the rest. On the server
they do nothing.

</note>

## Open it

- **Vue DevTools**: <kbd value="Alt">



</kbd>

 + <kbd value="Shift">



</kbd>

 + <kbd value="D">



</kbd>

, or the Vue button at
the bottom of the page, then the **Vue DnD Kit** tab.
- **Nuxt DevTools**: <kbd value="Alt">



</kbd>

 + <kbd value="Shift">



</kbd>

 + <kbd value="D">



</kbd>

, or the Nuxt button,
then **Vue DnD Kit** (in the sidebar or its overflow menu).
- **A window of its own**: open `http://localhost:5173/__vue-dnd-kit-devtools/` on your dev server,
or the tab's ⧉ button. Handy on a second screen. With several pages open, a select on top
chooses the one to watch.

<warning>

Keep the tab in a window of its own, not in a background browser tab of the same window: the page
must stay visible, and a hidden page cancels drags.

</warning>

## The mini-map

A live card per list, tree and drop target, with copies of their items where they are — the same
clones the overlay would show, with the page's CSS. During a drag it marks:

- the lists and targets that **accept** the drag (blue) or **refuse** it (red);
- the placeholder, and the target under the pointer;
- the pointer, the overlay's box, and the insertion line of `placeholder: 'indicator'` lists.

A click chooses an item and highlights it on the page; a double click scrolls the page to it. Use
the map when a drop doesn't go where you expect: it shows at a glance which lists take the drag.

## Drive: the joystick

Choose an item — on the map, in the registry, or with **⌖ Pick**, which takes the next press on a
draggable of the page instead of letting it act — and push the joystick's knob. The item is picked
up and moves that way, faster the farther the knob is from the center. Let go and it stops;
**Drop** and **Cancel** end the drag.

It is a real pointer drag of a sensor named `devtools`, made with the public
[sensor API](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/sensors#a-sensor-of-your-own): lists sort under it, containers
auto-scroll at their edges, and `onBeforeDrop` and `onDrop` run as for any drag. Disabled items
aren't picked up. A keyboard drag the page started can be steered too.

Items of sortable lists also get buttons: up, down, to the start, to the end, to another list of
the group. Each is one keyboard drag of [`moveItem`](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/sensors#programmatic-drags).
Below the joystick, a large copy of what the overlay shows.

An edit applies at once, to this page only, and is never written to your code: the library reads
the new value where it reads the option. It lasts until you reset it (↺ per option, or the reset in
the top bar), the provider unmounts or the page reloads. An edited option shows your code's value
next to it. Items mounted while an edit is set — rows of a virtual list — get it too.

## State

What each provider knows, for the node you chose:

- the **drag session**: status, the active ids, items and sensor, the target and whether it
accepts, the pointer, the overlay, the sortable group's session and insertion line;
- a **list**: its order and its draft; a **tree**: its rows;
- an **item**: its type, data and position; a **drop target**: its rules.

Items mount and unmount without events: the registry catches up within a second.

## Debug a drop, step by step

A card won't go into a column. With the tab open:

1. **Reproduce it** by hand, or with **Drive** so your hands stay free for the tab.
2. **Watch the map** while the card is over the column. Red means the list refuses the card: look at
its `group` (`put`) or the target's `accept`. Blue means it accepts, and the problem comes later.
3. **Read the log** of that drag. `onBeforeDrop` says who said no — a hook, or the target's
`accept`. If the drop went through but your data didn't change, the `drop` entry says whether
`preventDefault()` was called and what `e.result` held: a controlled list must apply it itself.
4. **Try a fix live** in **Options** — a looser `acceptMode`, another `collision`, `placeholder: 'indicator'` — then write the one that works into your code.

## How it works

Providers report to a hook that the page's side installs. Until a tab watches the page, they are
only recorded; then the page listens like any monitor and sends the tab what it shows — every
40 ms during a drag, twice a second otherwise — and stops once no tab has watched for a few
seconds. The tab talks to the page over a `BroadcastChannel` of the page's origin. It changes
nothing but what you ask for: the drags, the selection and the option overrides.

---

- **Page:** Files and other apps
- **Source:** https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/native
- **Description:** The browser's own drag and drop, as drags of the library — files, links and text from other apps into drop targets and lists that make room for them, items dragged out of the page, and between windows of your app.

The library's drags live inside the page. The browser has a drag and drop of its own that
crosses the page's edges: files from the desktop, a link from another tab, text from another
app, and items of yours dragged out to all of those. The library runs those drags too, as
drags of the provider: targets light up, lists make room, the events and the screen reader
texts are the usual ones.

<example height="34rem" hint="Drop images, links or text from other apps; drag a card out, or into this page in a second window" name="moodboard">



</example>

them.

const { items } = makeSortableList(grid, {
  items: cards,
  group: 'moodboard',
  strategy: 'grid',
  external: { files: 'image/*', links: true, text: true },
  createItem: fromOutside,
});
```

### Into a list

A list makes room for it as for a plain draggable: with `createItem`, which is asked twice:
while the drag is held, for the item that shows where it goes, and at the drop, with the
data, for what goes in. A list of items inserts them all at that place: a card per image.

```ts [cards.ts]
export const fromOutside = (active: Active): Card | Card[] | undefined => {
  const { external } = active;
  if (!external) return undefined;
  // While it is held: a tile that says what is coming.
  if (!external.ready) return { id: 'incoming', kind: 'incoming', label: incoming(external) };
  // At the drop: a card each.
  if (external.files.length) {
    return external.files.map((file) => ({ id: uid(), kind: 'image', src: URL.createObjectURL(file), name: file.name }));
  }
  if (external.urls.length) return external.urls.map((url) => ({ id: uid(), kind: 'link', url, title: host(url) }));
  const text = external.text.trim();
  return text ? { id: uid(), kind: 'note', text } : undefined;
};
```

- The incoming tile is a row of your list like any other: the list renders it, the rows
around it slide out of its way, `onDrop` gets the real ones.
- Trees take such drags too, one node at a time: a folder node with a child per file holds
several.
- The drop event has `e.external` with the data, in the list's `onDrop` as in the monitors'.

## Out of the page

With `native`, a mouse drag of an item is the browser's own drag, so it can leave the page:
onto the desktop, into an editor, a chat, another tab.

```ts [Tile.vue]
makeSortableItem(el, {
  item: () => props.card,
  native: { data: () => toOutside(props.card) },
});
```

```ts [cards.ts]
case 'link':
  return { 'text/uri-list': card.url, 'text/plain': card.url };
case 'note':
  return { 'text/plain': card.text };
```

- `data` gives other apps the item as MIME types and text: `text/plain`, `text/uri-list`,
`text/html`. Read when the drag starts. Without it, `native: true` carries the `label` as
text.
- On the page, the drag works as any other: targets, lists that make room, the drop. The
browser draws the dragged image instead of the overlay, and the element stays in place
(`transform` stays `null` with `overlay: false`).
- Touch and keyboard drags of the item stay the library's: the browser has no drag of its own
for them.
- `effect` (`effectAllowed`) says what the place it is dropped on may do: `'copyMove'` by
default. A drop elsewhere ends the drag with `droppedOutside`, `'move'`, `'copy'` or
`'link'`, in `onDragEnd`. A move takes the items out of their list; a copy leaves them.

`makeDraggable` takes `native` the same way.

## Between windows

An item with `native` also carries itself: the lists of its group in another window of your
app take it as if it came from one of their own lists. Open the moodboard in a second window
and drag a card across.

- While it is held, the other window already has the item: its list shows it in place.
- At the drop it goes in, and here it leaves its list (the drop was a move). Hold
<kbd value="Ctrl">



</kbd>

 (<kbd value="Option">



</kbd>

 on a Mac) to copy it instead.
- A list with `createItem` is asked for such items too, with `active.external.group` set and
the items in `active.items[].item`: return them, or copies with keys of that window.
Without `createItem`, they go in as they are.
- Items travel as JSON: dates become strings, functions are left out.

## Limits

- The data comes with the drop only, never before: plan the item that shows while a drag is
held without it.
- Dragging files is for mouse and trackpad users. Offer an `<input type="file">` next to the
zone too.
- One provider of the page takes drags from outside: the first that has a target for them.
- In Firefox, an item moved into another list during the drag and then dropped in another
window doesn't hear about that drop: it stays where it was here.
- An item whose JSON passes 16 KB still goes to another window, but that window shows it only
at the drop.

The API is in [makeDroppable](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/api/make-droppable#from-outside-the-page) and
[makeDraggable](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/api/make-draggable#out-of-the-page).

---

- **Page:** Sensors and programmatic drags
- **Source:** https://zizigy.github.io/vue-dnd-kit/docs/guides/sensors
- **Description:** How input becomes a drag — the pointer and keyboard sensors, activation constraints, canDrag, sensors of your own, and drags you script with @vue-dnd-kit/actions.

A sensor turns input into drags. It only tells the provider "drag this item from here", then where
the input moved, and whether it dropped or cancelled. The provider does the rest, the same way for
every sensor: one drag at a time, disabled items refused, activation constraints, sorting,
auto-scroll, announcements, <kbd value="Escape">



</kbd>

 and the whole drop.

Both run by default. The provider's `sensors` replaces the list:

```vue
<DnDProvider :sensors="[pointerSensor, keyboardSensor, joystick.sensor]">
```

To turn keyboard drags off, prefer `:keyboard="false"` to leaving `keyboardSensor` out: the
keyboard sensor is also what cancels any drag with <kbd value="Escape">



</kbd>

. Its keys are rebound with
`keyboard.keys` (see [Accessibility](https://zizigy.github.io/docs/guides/accessibility#the-keyboard)).

## Activation constraints

A press doesn't drag at once: it waits for its activation constraint, so a click stays a click and a
swipe can still scroll the page. Switch the rules of this list and press a row:

<example height="34.5rem" hint="Hold a row until the ring closes, or switch the rule" name="activation-modes">



</example>

A constraint has three fields:

<table>
<thead>
  <tr>
    <th>
      Field
    </th>

    </th>
  </tr>

      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      Once the press has lasted that many ms. With <code>
        distance
      </code>
      
       too, whichever comes first.
    </td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td>
      <code>
        tolerance
      </code>
    </td>
    
    <td>
      With <code>

      </code>
      
      : how far the pointer may move meanwhile. Past it the press gives up, so the page can scroll. Default 5 px when there is no <code>

      </code>
      
      .

  </tr>

Without your own, each pointer kind has its default:

<table>

      </code>
